papers.title: Propolis loading governs the morphology, stability, and wound-relevant bioactivity of electrospun PVA/gelatin nanofiber membranes
papers.abstract: Electrospun poly(vinyl alcohol)/gelatin (PVA/gelatin) nanofiber membranes containing 0–2.0% (v/v) propolis were fabricated to investigate how propolis loading governs membrane morphology, stability, and wound-relevant bioactivity. Increasing propolis concentration increased the mean fiber diameter from 170 ± 75 to 596 ± 453 nm and promoted partial fiber fusion at higher loadings. FTIR confirmed propolis incorporation, while DSC and TGA showed concentration-dependent changes in thermal behavior; T 50 increased from 349.78 °C for the propolis-free membrane to 427.12–446.70 °C after propolis incorporation. Propolis also altered aqueous behavior, with intermediate loadings showing markedly lower degradability. Lower to moderate propolis loading supported higher fibroblast viability, whereas higher loading generally enhanced cell migration and DPPH/ABTS radical-scavenging activity. Propolis-containing membranes reduced LPS-induced nitrite production in RAW 264.7 macrophages, although the response was formulation-dependent. Qualitative disc-diffusion screening showed detectable inhibition against Staphylococcus aureus from PG05P onward and against Pseudomonas aeruginosa at PG15P and PG20P. PG10P provided a favorable balance among morphology, aqueous stability, thermal stability, and measured biological responses. These findings provide an initial structure–stability–bioactivity framework, while mechanical suitability, propolis release kinetics, and quantitative antimicrobial potency remain to be established.

papers.title: Conformationally Locked AIE Chromophores in Organotin Coordination Networks for Enhanced Two‐Photon‐Excited Fluorescence
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient two‐photon‐excited fluorescence (TPEF) in crystalline frameworks requires compact, ordered chromophore organization while suppressing nonradiative decay from uncontrolled aggregation. Herein, tetranuclear organotin clusters were used to regulate the spatial arrangement and intramolecular rotation of tetraphenylethylene (TPE) chromophores. Two organotin coordination networks, OCN‐1 and OCN‐2, were synthesized from TPE‐based carboxylate ligands and tetranuclear organotin clusters. OCN‐1 adopts a 3D entangled architecture of interwoven 2D (4, 4)‐grid layers, whereas OCN‐2 comprises densely staggered 1D coordination chains. In both structures, coordination anchoring and short‐range contacts involving adjacent phenyl groups and tin‐bound alkyl substituents restrict aromatic rotation. Consequently, OCN‐1 and OCN‐2 achieved high solid‐state photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) of 92% and 95%, respectively. The hydrophobic organotin internal surface further imparted superhydrophobicity, broad aqueous stability, and negligible PL quenching under high‐humidity. Under 800 nm femtosecond excitation, OCN‐1 exhibited a pronounced TPEF response with an apparent two‐photon absorption cross section ( σ 2 , app) of approximately 4755 GM. In colloidal dispersions, its σ 2 , app was nearly 7.3‐fold higher than that of H 4 ETTC aggregates under identical conditions. These findings establish organotin‐directed chromophore packing as an effective strategy for converting AIE chromophore aggregation into moisture‐resistant crystalline materials with enhanced nonlinear fluorescence.

papers.title: The COMPARATIVE PHARMACOLOGICAL EVALUATION OF DOLICHOS ACIPHYLLUS EXTRACT AND ITS LIPID-BASED FORMULATION IN EXPERIMENTAL HYPERLIPIDEMIA
papers.journal: Asian Journal of Pharmaceutical and Clinical Research
papers.abstract: Objective: The major aim of the current research work was to analyze the antihyperlipidemic and antioxidant efficacy of Dolichos aciphyllus extract (DAE) and its prepared lipid-based formulation (Dolichos aciphyllus extract-loaded nanostructured lipid carriers [DAENLCs]) against the high-fat diet (HFD)-induced hyperlipidemic rats. Methods: Antihyperlipidemic efficacy of DAE was analyzed initially by in vitro 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase inhibition. HFD was used to induce hyperlipidemia in Wistar albino rats, followed by oral administration of DAE (400 mg/kg) and DAENLCs (400 mg/kg). The serum lipid parameters, such as cholesterol, triglycerides (TG), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), and very low-density lipoprotein (VLDL), were analyzed. Oxidative stress markers were determined by estimating malondialdehyde (MDA), reduced glutathione (GSH), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and catalase (CAT). Liver function markers, such as aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT), were also assessed, along with histopathological changes in liver and adipose tissue, together with phytochemical screening and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) fingerprinting for identifying the major phytochemical constituents. Results: The recent study showed that DAE and DAENLCs have marked in vitro HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor activity, followed by the lipid-based formulation showing greater inhibition than the pure extract. Treatment with a high dose of DAE and DAENLCs in HFD-induced hyperlipidemic rats showed a considerable reduction in the levels of serum total cholesterol, TG, LDL, VLDL, and atherogenic index while increasing the HDL levels when compared with the control group. The levels of AST and ALT, along with MDA levels, were also reduced considerably in the treatment groups when compared to the standard drug atorvastatin, while restoring the GSH, SOD, and CAT activities. The histopathological results showed improvement in the liver structure and morphology of adipose tissue in the treatment groups, where DAENLC demonstrated better protection of the tissue than DAE. The presence of quercetin in DAE was confirmed by the preliminary HPLC fingerprinting analysis by comparison with the standard quercetin. Conclusion: DAE showed potential antihyperlipidemia and antioxidant efficacy in hyperlipidemic rats, which was further increased when formulated in a lipid-based formulation. DAENLC showed improvement in lipid metabolism, oxidative stress, liver function, and alterations in liver architecture when compared with the pure extract. Thus, DAENLCs showed an enhanced pharmacological activity of Dolichos aciphyllus, which makes DAENLC a promising phyto-pharmaceutical strategy for treating hyperlipidemia and other metabolic disorders.

papers.title: Intercalation of O2, H2, and CO beneath epitaxial graphene on Ir(111): A review of atomic-scale decoupling mechanisms and pathways to catalysis, sensing, and energy applications
papers.abstract: Intercalation of gases and metal species beneath graphene supported on transition-metal substrates has emerged as a powerful strategy for tuning graphene–substrate interactions and tailoring its electronic, chemical, and mechanical properties. Numerous studies have investigated these phenomena using surface-sensitive techniques, including X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), and low-energy electron diffraction (LEED). This review examines the intercalation of oxygen, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen, with particular emphasis on graphene grown on Ir(111). Oxygen intercalation proceeds under ultrahigh-vacuum conditions through atomic oxygen formation on bare Ir terraces and requires elevated temperatures (~355 K), whereas hydrogen intercalation occurs at much lower temperatures (~140 K). CO intercalation takes place near room temperature but requires millibar-range pressures. In all cases, substrate step edges and graphene flake boundaries serve as critical pathways for intercalant penetration. These structural features have been consistently identified as key entry points for intercalant diffusion. Intercalation provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling the properties of 2D materials, enabling modulation of electrical conductivity, thermoelectric response, and catalytic activity. The process significantly modifies the electronic, chemical, and mechanical characteristics of the graphene layer, while also partially decoupling it from the underlying substrate. Given these effects, gas intercalation beneath graphene represents a promising strategy for applications in catalysis, sensing, and energy storage. Intercalation can also be used to partially separate the graphene overlayer from the underlying metal, leading to considerable enhancement of electronic, chemical and mechanical properties. This review highlights the fundamental mechanisms and technological potential of gas (O 2 , H 2 , and CO) intercalation beneath graphene for applications in catalysis, sensing, energy storage, and next-generation graphene-based devices.

papers.title: Dual-waste valorisation of pine needle biomass and post-consumer PET into sustainable composites: Mechanical, dynamic mechanical and environmental performance
papers.journal: Plastics Rubber and Composites Macromolecular Engineering
papers.abstract: The use of lignocellulosic biomass with post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is an attractive option for waste diversion and resource recovery. In this study, pine needle (PN) biomass was used to reinforce a commercial unsaturated polyester resin (UPR) made from recycled PET (rPET). The untreated (UPN) and NaOH-treated (TPN) fibres were added at 30 wt% using the vacuum-bagging method and subsequently characterised by tensile and flexural testing, dynamic mechanical analysis, Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscope (SEM), and 45-day water immersion and soil burial ageing. Alkali treatment raised tensile strength from 7.32 ± 0.46 to 11.05 ± 0.53 MPa (+50.9%), flexural strength from 44.00 ± 3.16 to 64.20 ± 6.10 MPa (+45.9%), and the moisture-diffusion coefficient fell from 9.81 × 10 −13 to 3.76 × 10 −13 m 2 s −1 . TPN-rPET was superior to UPN-rPET under environmental ageing conditions. Alkaline modification, therefore, improves PN reinforcement, resulting in a waste-based composite material suitable for non-load-bearing and lightly loaded applications.

papers.title: Development and Characterization of Novel Bio‐Based Films Based on Sodium Alginate and Pineapple Crown Waste: Effects of Emulsion Integration and Matrix Formulation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The ubiquitous application of conventional petroleum‐derived polymers has precipitated a severe global environmental crisis, driving the urgent need for bio‐based alternatives. To address this challenge, novel biopolymeric films were developed utilizing a crosslinked sodium alginate matrix reinforced with upcycled pineapple crown waste and structurally modified by a Tween 20‐stabilized coconut oil emulsion. The composite films were fabricated via the conventional solvent casting technique, and their formulation was systematically optimized using a Central Composite Rotatable Design (CCRD). Experimental analysis revealed that the optimal formulation, characterized by a restricted glycerol concentration and the inclusion of the lipidic emulsion, exhibited significantly reduced water solubility and moisture retention. The incorporation of the lipid domains within the biopolymer network, as suggested by structural and morphological observations, mitigated the inherent hydrophilicity of the matrix, yielding a more compact and seemingly homogeneous microarchitecture. Furthermore, the formulation containing the stabilized lipidic phase exhibited enhanced high‐temperature stability and degradation resistance, which may be associated with a potential thermal shielding effect and altered char formation. Ultimately, these emulsion‐stabilized biocomposites present a promising bio‐based alternative for the packaging industry, with potential applications in the circular bioeconomy through the valorization of agricultural waste.

papers.title: Docking Simulation and Artificial-Intelligence-Assisted Molecularly Imprinted Polymer Electrochemical Sensor for the Detection of Cancer Biomarkers
papers.abstract: Abstract Cancer remains one of the leading life-threatening diseases worldwide, and therefore, early stage detection of cancer biomarkers is vital for effective diagnosis and treatment planning. Conventional detection techniques primarily rely on biological recognition elements, including enzymes, antibodies, aptamers, DNA, RNA; however, these elements are often prone to denaturation and have limited stability under extreme environmental conditions and long-term storage. To overcome these obstacles, molecularly imprinted polymers have emerged as a promising alternative to traditional biorecognition elements because of the ease of synthesis, low expenditure, and relative stability. In addition, MIP-based electrochemical sensors prove their applicability in detecting various disease biomarkers in general and cancer biomarkers in particular. This study presents an overview of MIPs and MIP-based electrochemical sensors, with a particular focus on their application in cancer biomarkers detection. Representative studies are discussed in detail to illustrate the structure and efficacy of these systems. In particular, strategies for improving imprinting factors of the molecular docking and artificial-intelligence-assisted MIP-electrochemical sensors up to 6.45- or 3-fold higher compared to the conventional approaches are considered in detail. Finally, current limitations and challenges, as well as future perspectives and potential solutions, are critically discussed and proposed.

papers.title: Deep Eutectic Solvents as PVDF-HFP Membrane Modifiers: Morphology, Performance, and Fouling Impact in Gas–Liquid Methane Recovery from Anaerobic Effluents
papers.abstract: Abstract Dissolved methane (D-CH4) emissions from anaerobic effluents constitute an energy loss and a source of greenhouse gas emissions, and its recovery by polymeric membranes can be hindered by fouling. In this work, the long-term performance under realistic conditions of poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) membranes fabricated with dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) as a nontoxic solvent and deep eutectic solvents (DES) as membrane modifiers via non-solvent-induced phase separation was evaluated. An analysis based on Hansen solubility parameters showed the role of polymer–solvent–additive interaction in membrane formation. The moderate affinity between PVDF-HFP and DMSO promoted fast liquid–liquid demixing, yielding porous structures with low crystallinity. The addition of DES modified phase inversion kinetics, increasing porosity and enabling variations in pore size and crystalline phase composition. Choline chloride-based DES (ChCl:glycerol, ChCl:urea and ChCl:ethylene glycol) enhanced the formation of the β-phase fraction from 0.68 to 0.85 and reduced the pore size from 0.44 to 0.23–0.32 μm, whereas thymol:menthol DES promoted larger pores of 0.54 ± 0.01 μm and α-phase fraction, evidencing the key role of additive polarity in solid–liquid demixing. All fabricated membranes exhibited D-CH4 removal efficiency (RE) profiles fully comparable to those of commercial PVDF (≈36%), achieving a RE at 5 h in the range of 36.4–41.7%. Long-term tests using the anaerobic effluent revealed a progressive RE decline to ≈20% in both the pristine membrane and with ChCl:EG due to fouling, with the latter showing a less pronounced RE decline during the initial hours (<100 h), though the final RE at 300 h was similar. The performance decline was due to surface deposition of organic foulants (extracellular polymeric substances and fatty acids) and inorganic salts, and the ultrasonic-driven cleaning process with water and citric acid partially removed the fouling. Overall, this study demonstrates that nontoxic DMSO with DES addition could replace hazardous traditional solvents in membrane fabrication without compromising D-CH4 RE.

papers.title: Divergent Ultrafast Carrier-Density and Photoconductivity Dynamics in Antimony-Doped Halide Perovskite Thin Films
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abstract: Abstract Heterovalent ion substitution can tune the optoelectronic properties of metal halide perovskites, but its impact on charge-carrier recombination and transport remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate antimony incorporation in methylammonium lead iodide (MAPI) thin films using complementary ultrafast spectroscopy techniques. Optical absorption shows that the bandgap remains approximately 1.61 eV across substitution levels up to 10%, whereas photoluminescence and transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy reveal increasing nonradiative recombination rates with increasing antimony content. Optical pump–terahertz probe (OPTP) spectroscopy further uncovers fluence-dependent dynamics distinct from TA that are absent in pristine MAPI. After considering alternative mechanisms, we interpret this behavior as consistent with partially heterogeneous transport, in which Sb3+ incorporation may introduce low-mobility, defect-rich regions within a higher-mobility crystalline network. Thus, heterovalent substitution can introduce hidden transport losses without changing optical bandgap, highlighting the importance of mobility-sensitive measurements to probe doped perovskite films.

papers.title: Performance of sustainable ultra-high-performance concrete with microplastics: comparative strategies of nano-coated microplastics and direct nanomaterial incorporation
papers.abstract: Abstract Microplastics (MPs) are pervasive environmental contaminants with increasing urgency for sustainable management strategies. Their incorporation into cementitious materials offers a promising pathway for waste valorization; however, the weak interfacial transition zone (ITZ) between MPs and the cement matrix severely limits mechanical performance and hinders structural applications. This study presents a comparative nano-engineering framework to overcome this limitation by systematically evaluating two fundamentally distinct strategies: (1) direct surface nano-coating of MPs using a nano-silica and cellulose nanocrystal system, and (2) matrix nano-densification through direct incorporation of the same nanomaterials into ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC). Because these two strategies deliver nanomaterials in fundamentally different ways, a fair comparison required equating their nanomaterial content. This was achieved by using thermogravimetric analysis to quantify the nanomaterial mass retained on the MP surface and applying the same content to the nano-densification mixtures. A comprehensive experimental program was conducted across multiple MP replacement levels (10–50%) to elucidate the effects of these strategies on mechanical performance and interfacial behavior. Results show that MP incorporation significantly reduces strength due to weak interfacial bonding and increased porosity; however, both nano-engineering approaches effectively recover performance by enhancing ITZ integrity. Notably, despite a 50% MP replacement, the optimized mixtures achieved a compressive strength of 91 MPa, demonstrating structural-level performance using high volumes of plastic waste. While both strategies yielded comparable mechanical improvements, matrix nano-densification provided slightly higher strength gains, whereas nano-coated MPs exhibited superior workability and required substantially less high-range water reducer to achieve equivalent workability, indicating superior and practical scalability. The study advances the field by providing the first direct comparison between ITZ-targeted nano-coating and matrix-level nano-densification for MP-modified UHPC, revealing that although both strategies achieve comparable mechanical performance, they differ substantially in admixture demand. These findings establish an application-oriented pathway for integrating microplastic waste into high-performance structural materials, contributing to circular material design and sustainable infrastructure development.

papers.title: Vanadium Distribution and Competing Slag Associations in Reductive Smelting of Spent NiMoV Catalysts: Oxygen Potential, Aluminosilicate Interactions, and Metal Recovery Constraints—A Critical Review
papers.journal: Journal International Review of Research Studies
papers.abstract: Spent Ni–Mo–V hydroprocessing catalysts are alumina-rich secondary resources whose reduction smelting produces valuable metal alloys and complex oxide slags. This critical narrative review addresses where vanadium resides when it is not recovered in the bulk alloy. It contrasts direct experimental evidence with thermodynamic and mechanistic analogs, explicitly separating vanadium dissolved in liquid slag, retained in crystalline oxides, entrained as metallic droplets, and transferred to dust or deposits. Under different operating configurations, reported V recoveries range from 25.1% in reduction–sulfurization smelting to 89.7% in reduction smelting of mixed catalyst/ore feeds; an independent optimized kilogram-scale catalyst-smelting study reported 97.9%. These process recoveries are not equilibrium partition coefficients and cannot be transferred across feed and slag systems. We formalize phase-specific vanadium inventories, recovery, and mass-balance closure, and assess the coupled roles of oxygen potential, carbon and sulfur activities, aluminosilicate chemistry, crystallization, liquidus margin, and droplet settling. The review presents a diagnosis-first framework for distinguishing chemical retention from physical separation losses and identifies the experimental data needed for process optimization and scale-up.

papers.title: Chain Length, Unsaturation, and Conformational State Modulate ω-3 FFA Effects on POPC Bilayers
papers.abstract: Abstract Free fatty acids (FFAs), specifically the ω-3 forms α-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), are important modulators of lipid membrane structure and dynamics, yet how these three species compare within a single, consistent framework remains unclear. Here, we employed atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the effects of ALA, EPA, and DHA (5–20 mol %) on 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (POPC) bilayers in single-FFA and mixed DHA/EPA systems. FFA incorporation induces concentration-dependent bilayer condensation, marked by decreased area and volume per lipid, increased thickness, and enhanced acyl chain order, with ALA producing the strongest effects. All three FFAs promote reorientation of POPC headgroups toward embedded FFA carboxyl groups. Using a conformational classification scheme (stretched, intermediate, coiled), we show that local ordering of neighboring POPC chains and the FFAs’ own ordering strongly depend on conformational state. FFAs exhibit higher lateral mobility than POPC. Passive transbilayer diffusion depends on FFA type and concentration; only ALA is nonmonotonic. In mixed DHA/EPA systems, lateral diffusion of EPA is enhanced relative to single-FFA systems, whereas passive diffusion of DHA is reduced. These results show that chain length and unsaturation mainly modulate FFA effects on bilayer structure and dynamics, whereas conformational state additionally shapes local acyl-chain ordering, relevant to membrane behavior under elevated and pathological FFA levels.

papers.title: Preparation and properties of gel polymer electrolytes based on tetrafunctional cross-linked PEG network
papers.abstract: Abstract Thiol-yne click reaction between pentaerythritol tetrakis(3-mercaptopropionate) and α, ω-dipropiolate-terminated polyethylene glycol was carried out in propylene carbonate containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imideto obtain gel polymer electrolyte with tetra-branched network structure. The ionic conductivity was found to depend on the polymer content in the gel polymer electrolyte and the chain length of the polyethylene glycol constituting the tetra-branched network structure. These experimental results indicated that lithium cations moved not only within the electrolyte solution but also along the PEG chains that form a network structure.

papers.title: Cold atmospheric pressure plasma pretreatment as a novel tool to tailor the functional properties of quince seed mucilage biopolymer-based edible films
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Quince seed mucilage (QSM) is a promising polysaccharide for the fabrication of biodegradable edible films; however, its relatively limited functional performance restricts broader food-packaging applications. Scope and Approach: The present study investigated the effects of cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) treatment applied to QSM solutions at 6, 7, and 8 kV for 1, 3, and 5 min, followed by a comprehensive evaluation of the physicochemical, surface, barrier, mechanical, and thermal properties of the resulting films. Key Findings: CAP treatment did not significantly affect film thickness regardless of the applied processing conditions. Contact angle analysis demonstrated that the highest surface hydrophobicity was achieved under a 7 kV for 3 min plasma treatment. Water vapor barrier measurements revealed that films treated for 3 min exhibited the lowest permeability, irrespective of the applied voltage. Surface topography analysis indicated that 6 kV for 1min plasma exposure generated the greatest surface roughness, whereas increasing either the treatment duration or applied voltage produced a denser, more homogeneous, and compact film microstructure. Compared with the untreated control, CAP treatment significantly enhanced the mechanical performance of the films, with the optimum tensile properties obtained following treatment at 6 kV for 1 min. Thermal characterization by TGA and DSC further demonstrated that 5 min plasma exposure time adversely affected the thermal stability of the films, while optimized CAP conditions (3 min) provided the most favorable thermal performance. Conclusions Overall, the findings demonstrate that appropriately optimized CAP treatment effectively improves the structural integrity and functional performance of QSM-based biodegradable films.

papers.title: Modulating Sulfur Composition toward Ultralow Dielectric Loss Polymers: A Miscible Blending Strategy with Poly(phenylene oxide)/Poly(phenylene sulfide) Alternating Copolymers
papers.abstract: Abstract In recent high-speed communications (i.e., 5G and 6G), insulating polymers exhibiting both a minimized dielectric constant (Dk) and dissipation factor (Df) have been extensively used to reduce dielectric loss, although the empirical Dk–Df trade-off relationship has prevented further reductions in these values. Here, we describe a rational approach for the simultaneous reduction of both Dk and Df through simple polymer blending, wherein a low-Dk ether polymer is hybridized with a low-Df sulfide polymer. Specifically, upon mixing poly(2,6-dimethyl-1,4-phenylene sulfide) (PMPS) or poly(2,6-dimethyl-1,4-phenylene oxide) (PPO) with their alternating copolymer, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) thermograms of the resulting polymer blends revealed their miscibility, as verified by shifting of glass-transition temperatures, allowing for the successful film preparation and the tuning of their dielectric properties without compromising other material properties (e.g., thermostability). In particular, the observed enhancement in free fractional volume for the polymer blends suggests a reduction in Dk, finally minimizing dielectric loss (Dk = 2.43, Df = 0.00081 at 10 GHz). Specifically, those dielectric losses are significantly lower than the empirical limits defined for single-component polymers. Overall, this study describes a rational strategy for the preparation of diverse insulating polymers with extremely low dielectric losses.

papers.title: Physiology‐Informed Layered Sensing for Intelligent Human–Exoskeleton Interaction
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable exoskeletons offer substantial potential to enhance human mobility in everyday environments. However, their translation beyond laboratory environments remains limited by sensing systems that capture movement but not underlying physiology. Here, we introduce a physiology‐layered perception framework for wearable exoskeletons that aligns sensing and inference with the bone–muscle–skin hierarchy to provide task‐specific physiological cues for assistance, effort optimization, and safety co‐monitoring. The framework maps inertial measurement units (IMUs) to skeletal kinematics, surface electromyography (sEMG) to muscular activation, and strain to cutaneous deformation, with real‐time neural decoders tailored to each objective. As a system‐level demonstration of this framework, we implement it in a soft, lightweight smart‐textile platform integrated with a portable ankle exoskeleton (on‐body sensing and electronics weighing < 20 g). Under leave‐one‐subject‐out evaluation on unseen users, the platform achieves accurate ankle joint‐moment estimation (RMSE = 0.13 Nm kg −1 ), real‐time classification of metabolic trends (96.3% accuracy), and sub‐100 ms detection of injury‐related risk (recall = 0.96). This work establishes a physiology‐aligned sensing architecture that reframes exoskeleton perception from motion tracking to real‐time physiological decoding, offering a pathway toward intelligent, adaptive, and personalized wearable robotics.

papers.title: Multiomics Integration Reveals a Skeletal Muscle Metabolic Myopathy in Cardiometabolic HFpEF
papers.abstract: Background: Skeletal muscle dysfunction is a major peripheral determinant of exercise intolerance and physical disability in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Metabolic and mitochondrial dysfunction are considered to be key components of skeletal muscle dysfunction, but comprehensive profiling of metabolic pathways has not been conducted. Elucidation of dysregulated metabolic pathways is essential to determine viable targets for the treatment of exercise intolerance in HFpEF. Methods: was used to determine differential expression in all omics layers (absolute fold-change>1.5, FDR0.05, unless otherwise indicated). Additional targeted plasma and skeletal muscle (soleus and EDL) metabolomics and lipidomics were performed on HFpEF and control rats. Results: Pathway level analysis for RNA seq and proteomics revealed significant downregulation of oxidative phosphorylation (NES -2.1, p<0.005), electron transport chain (NES -2.0, p<0.005), and TCA cycle (-1.8, p<0.05). The most upregulated pathways were PPAR signaling (NES 2.2, p<0.0001), tryptophan metabolism (NES 1.8, P<0.005), and amino acid oxidation (NES 1.8, p<0.005) pathways. Metabolomics revealed an accumulation of TCA cycle intermediate, isocitrate, and phosphate reduction. Branched-chain amino acids were significantly increased, whereas amino acids related to tryptophan metabolism were reduced and shifted towards increased serotonin accumulation. Phospholipid species were differentially regulated with increased palmitoylated phosphatidylcholines but reduced arachidonoyl-PC species. Phosphatidylethanolamines (PE) species (16:0/16:1-18:0/18:2) were increased. Conclusion: Our multiomics analysis of skeletal muscle in HFpEF revealed severe mitochondrial dysfunction that was characterized by reduced complex I and II activity. Mitochondrial and peroxisomal lipid overload results in a shift in membrane phospholipid accumulation and composition. Reduced BCAA oxidation and dysregulation of tryptophan metabolism are key features of amino acid metabolism that reduce anaplerosis and promote the accumulation of toxic metabolites. Comparative analysis of other skeletal muscle disorders suggests that an acquired metabolic myopathy exists in cardiometabolic HFpEF.

papers.title: Intelligent optimization-based calibration of DEM numerical parameters using an improved sparrow search algorithm
papers.abstract: Abstract Calibration of meso parameters is the foundation of discrete element method (DEM) simulations. To overcome the limitations of the traditional trial-and-error calibration method, such as its time-consuming process and poor repeatability, this study proposes an efficient DEM meso parameters calibration method based on an improved sparrow search algorithm (ISSA). The algorithm integrates multiple enhancement strategies, including improved circle chaotic mapping for population initialization, adaptive inertia weight, Lévy flight, and Cauchy–Gaussian mutation. The results demonstrate that the proposed calibration method is applicable to multi-scale models and accurately reproduces both laboratory-scale specimen results and field-scale experimental observations. The laboratory-scale DEM simulation achieved parameter calibration with a total error of less than 1% within 4.4 hours, while the field-scale DEM simulation results showed discrepancies of only 0.21% in failure depth and 0.29% in failure range compared with field observations. Furthermore, under the same accuracy conditions, the ISSA exhibits a remarkable speed advantage in meso parameters calibration, outperforming the SSA-DEM, WOA-DEM, DA-DEM, and PSO-DEM algorithms by 83.33%, 128.57%, 226.19%, and 371.42%, respectively. These results confirm that the proposed calibration method achieves automated and efficient parameter identification for DEM under the guidance of intelligent optimization algorithms.

papers.title: Material Development and Characterization of Ductile Lunar and Martian Regolith-Based Cementitious Composite
papers.abstract: Abstract This study successfully develops lunar and Martian regolith-based strain-hardening cementitious composites (SHCC). Mixtures incorporated four different regolith simulants, lunar highlands (LH) and lunar mare (LM) for the Moon and Martian global (MG) and Martian polyhydrated-sulfate (MS) for Mars, with five formulations per celestial body at 65% by weight simulant replacement and 1% by volume polyethylene (PE) fibers. Characterization included calorimetry/thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), compressive and direct-tensile testing, crack-pattern analysis under both loading and unloading conditions, and particle-packing evaluation. Ductile Mooncrete achieved compressive strengths of 44–68 MPa and tensile ductility of 2.3%–5.7% with an ultimate strain of 4.9–7.2 MPa at peak stress, consistently coupling strength with ductility. Ductile Marscrete reached 31–50 MPa in compression and 4.4%–9.2% tensile strain at 3.2–5.9 MPa peak stress, showing composition-dependent tradeoffs between strength (MG-rich) and ductility (MS-rich). Crack mapping confirmed a multiple-cracking pattern without localization. Mooncrete exhibited fewer, tighter cracks while Marscrete showed higher crack multiplicity with wider openings, and both systems displayed measurable crack-width recovery upon unloading. These results demonstrate the feasibility of fabricating simulant based, strain-hardening composites from lunar and Martian regolith simulants and highlight composition as a lever to tune stiffness, strength, and ductility for resilient space infrastructure.

papers.title: Sustainable crop production under future climates: national mapping of cover-crop rotations and soil organic carbon–N2O trade-offs
papers.abstract: Abstract Sustainable crop production increasingly depends on rotation designs that raise productivity while lowering reactive nitrogen (N) losses and net greenhouse gases. We conduct a national, spatial analysis for Germany, evaluating diversified 4-year rotations with alternating legume/non-legume cover crops (CCs) under future climates (RCP4.5/8.5, six GCMs). Using the DSSAT crop–soil model coupled to dynamic Tier-2 N₂O accounting (driven by DSSAT-simulated fertilizer, residue, and leached N), we map impacts on yield, N use efficiency (NUE), N leaching, ΔSOC, and net GHG relative to business-as-usual rotations. Across the ensemble, legume-inclusive CC sequences increase cereal yields by ~16–33% (zone-dependent), improve NUE, and reduce N leaching by ~40%. Systems accrue additional SOC but approach plateaus over decades; N₂O responses are climate- and soil-contingent, yet the net GHG footprint falls by ~35–45% on average through 2099 when ΔSOC and direct + indirect N₂O are jointly considered. Accounting for upstream seed and diesel for CCs may slightly attenuates (but does not negate) the net benefit. Spatial “leverage maps” reveal where rotation redesign most robustly delivers the triad of higher production, lower N losses, and lower net GHG, and where trade-offs persist. Results provide policy-ready evidence that targeted, legume-inclusive cover-crop rotations can advance cleaner crop production in temperate regions under changing climate.

papers.title: Evolutionary dynamics of collective behavior across the tree of ray-finned fishes
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Abstract Trait evolution and lineage diversification are thought to be driven by selection on the phenotypes of individuals. However, many important phenotypes are only manifested when individuals interact. Collective behavior is one such phenotype. During collective behavior, interactions among individuals lead to emergent group-level phenotypes that can govern individual fitness. Yet, whether collective behaviors exhibit similar patterns of trait evolution to individual traits and whether these group phenotypes have influenced macroevolutionary diversification is unknown. In ray-finned fishes, the most species-rich of all vertebrate classes, many species exhibit striking displays of collective behavior in the form of collective movement. Here, we use state-of-the-art machine learning methods for text and image analysis to quantify collective movement phenotypes for 2,839 Actinopterygian fishes, comprising nearly 10% of all extant species. We find that collective movement is highly evolutionarily stable in some clades and extremely labile in others, exhibiting over 300 evolutionary transitions. Consistent with theoretical predictions, collective movement is associated with more patchy diets and higher predation pressure. Finally, we find that the evolution of collective movement coincides with an increase in net macroevolutionary diversification rate. Our analyses reveal that collective behavior is deeply intertwined with ecological and evolutionary dynamics across a vast phylogenetic scale, unlocking new questions about the role of collective phenotypes in shaping the diversity of life on Earth. Significance Collective behavior is thought to contribute to the fitness of individuals that live in groups, but we still do not understand why some species exhibit collective behavior and others do not. We developed machine learning methods to quantify collective phenotypes for thousands of species spanning the phylogeny of ray-finned fishes and found collective behavior to be widespread and consistently correlated with experiencing higher predation pressure and foraging for grouping prey. Lineages that evolve collective movement show a higher net diversification rate. Our results illustrate that collective behavior is foundational to the broad-scale patterns of evolution and diversification in the largest vertebrate class.

Our results illustrate that collective behavior is foundational to the broad-scale patterns of evolution and diversification in the largest vertebrate class.

papers.title: First-Principles Study of Structural, Electronic, Thermal, and Optical Properties of Quasi-2D C 2 N 2 O Using GGA and HSE06
papers.journal: International Journal of Modern Physics B
papers.abstract: DFT and AIMD are used to investigate the structural, stability, electronic, thermal, and optical properties of the quasi-2D C 2 N 2 O structure. The structure exhibits thermal and energy stability, signifying robustness under ambient conditions, however dynamical instability is observed. The electronic structure investigation reveals that C 2 N 2 O displays semiconducting properties with a moderate indirect band gap resulting from the hybridisation of p-orbitals of N, C, and O atoms, with band gap values of 2.3 eV (GGA) and 3.93 eV (HSE06). The optical properties, including the dielectric function, optical conductivity, and refractive index, are thoroughly analyzed to clarify the electronic transitions. The material exhibits considerable optical absorption in the visible and ultraviolet spectrum, with notable anisotropy between in-plane and out-of-plane polarizations. Furthermore, plasmon resonance occurs at around 14.3 eV, relating to the collective oscillations of charge carriers. The thermal properties indicate a heat capacity of around 382 J/mol.K at 300 K, which is close to and slightly above the standard Dulong-Petit limit for this structure, indicating near-complete excitation of lattice vibrational modes at room temperature. The lattice thermal conductivity is extremely low, reaching approximately 0.017 W/m.K at 300 K, primarily attributed to significant phonon scattering, evidenced by a scattering rate of roughly 3.2 1/ps in the phonon frequency ranges. The findings demonstrate that the C 2 N 2 O structure maintains structural stability while allowing for tunable electronic, optical, and thermal properties, making it a promising candidate for nanoscale optoelectronic and thermal control applications.

papers.title: Parametrically Driven iSWAP Gate Using a Capacitively Shunted Double-Transmon Coupler at the Zero-Flux Sweet Spot
papers.abstract: A double-transmon coupler (DTC) enables a fast, high-fidelity CZ gate between two highly detuned, fixed-frequency transmon qubits. Moreover, a recently proposed capacitively shunted DTC (CSDTC) realizes a small residual ZZ interaction over a wide flux-bias range around zero flux, eliminating the necessity of static flux biasing while maintaining high CZ-gate fidelity. However, CZ gates with the DTC and CSDTC require baseband flux pulses with large amplitudes, which are vulnerable to pulse distortion and decoherence due to large qubit-coupler hybridization. To address these issues, we experimentally demonstrate a parametrically driven iSWAP gate operated at zero flux bias between highly detuned, fixed-frequency transmon qubits coupled through a CSDTC. Using a simple flux-drive waveform without predistortion, we realize an average gate fidelity of 99.92(2)% at a total gate time of 112 ns. The observed high-fidelity performance is consistent with small qubit-coupler hybridization and small effective ZZ interaction during the gate. Our numerical simulations reproduce the experimentally observed iSWAP interaction rate and effective ZZ interaction, demonstrating the applicability of the theoretical model not only to spectral information but also to time-domain dynamics such as gate operations. These results boost further progress in the research of superconducting quantum computers.

The observed high-fidelity performance is consistent with small qubit-coupler hybridization and small effective ZZ interaction during the gate. These results boost further progress in the research of superconducting quantum computers.

papers.title: Selective recovery of lithium from spent lithium iron phosphate cathodes via Fenton reaction
papers.abstract: Abstract Recycling of spent lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries is essential for resource sustainability and environmental protection. However, conventional recycling methods often involve harsh conditions, sacrificial reagents, high energy consumption, and secondary pollution. This study proposes a novel and efficient lithium extraction method based on a photo-fenton process to selectively recover lithium from spent LiFePO₄ cathodes. Under optimized conditions (800 mmol/L H₂O₂, 100 mmol/L FeSO₄, 30°C, 50 g/L solid density, and 30 min reaction time), a lithium leaching efficiency exceeding 99% was achieved with high selectivity. During this process, iron and phosphorus were simultaneously recovered as FePO₄ precipitate, while lithium was subsequently separated as high-purity Li₂CO₃. Mechanistic investigations, supported by XRD, XPS, and SEM-EDS analyses, revealed that hydroxyl radicals (•OH), generated from the Fe²⁺/H₂O₂ Fenton system, attack the olivine structure of LiFePO₄. This oxidizes Fe(II) to Fe(III), forming insoluble FePO₄ and releasing Li⁺ into solution. Notably, ultraviolet irradiation facilitates the regeneration of Fe²⁺ from the reaction products, enabling its reuse and significantly reducing reagent consumption and iron sludge generation. The proposed photo-Fenton method offers an efficient, low-energy, and environmentally benign route for lithium recovery from spent LFP batteries.

papers.title: Inflammatory mechanism of COP1‑mediated low‑frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation in the treatment of epilepsy
papers.abstract: Objective The present study sought to uncover the underlying molecular mechanisms of low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (LF-rTMS) in epilepsy treatment. Methods In BV2 cells and status epilepticus (SE) mice, COP1 expression was manipulated by molecular approaches, and then LF-rTMS was applied. Then real time quantitative PCR, Western Blot, Immunofluorescence Staining and Elisa were performed. Results We observed that COP1 expression was markedly decreased in the hippocampus and microglia of SE mice. In vitro experiments revealed that overexpression of COP1 (OE-COP1) notably reduced PILO-induced microglial activation as assessed by IBA1 expression. In vivo, OE-COP1 alleviated oxidative stress and downregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines in SE mice. Moreover, LF-rTMS treatment notably increased COP1 expression and inhibited C/EBPβ expression in the hippocampus of SE mice; knockdown of COP1 (sh-COP1) abolished these effects. Further validation demonstrated that LF-rTMS reduced microglial activation, oxidative stress, and pro-inflammatory cytokine levels in SE mice by promoting COP1 expression. Conclusions Our findings identify COP1 as a key mediator through which LF-rTMS exerts its therapeutic effects in epilepsy treatment, namely by upregulating COP1 to inhibit neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. This study establishes a novel molecular basis for applying LF-rTMS clinically in epilepsy.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and green supply chain management in Chinese listed firms
papers.abstract: Abstract As the core driving force of the new generation of industrial revolution, artificial intelligence technology has brought new opportunities for empowering enterprise green transformation and advancing sustainability. Focusing on Chinese A-share listed companies and based on unbalanced panel data from 2016 to 2024, this study systematically examines the impact, transmission mechanisms, and heterogeneity of AI applications on green supply chain management (GSCM). Drawing on the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities theory, this paper constructs an integrated theoretical framework that traces a causal link between AI applications through firm internal capabilities to green supply chain management. The empirical results show that AI applications significantly promote GSCM. Mechanism tests reveal that AI indirectly enhances GSCM by improving four dimensions of firm internal capabilities: green innovation, ESG performance, supply chain efficiency, and resource integration. In addition, heterogeneity analysis indicates that the enabling effect of AI on GSCM is more pronounced in state-owned enterprises, firms with higher environmental information disclosure quality, and firms in heavily polluting industries. This study deepens theoretical understanding of the relationship between AI and GSCM, reveals the micro-mechanisms and boundary conditions of AI-enabled GSCM, and provides practical insights for policymakers to guide firms in strategically applying AI and building efficient and collaborative green supply chains.

papers.title: Integrated metabolomics and transcriptomics analyses characterize the tissue-specific flavonoid biosynthesis and quality formation in the ethnomedicine Melastoma dodecandrum
papers.abstract: Melastoma dodecandrum Lour. is a prominent medicinal plant traditionally utilized in the southern China for treating gynecological inflammation disorders, representing significant potential for pharmaceutical development. However, systematic phytochemical characterization of this species remains incomplete, and the tissue-specific distribution and accumulation of its primary bio-activeflavonoids remain unclear. In this study, an integrated untargeted metabolomics and transcriptomic approach was employed to systematically elucidate the spatial distribution of flavonoids across the roots, stems, and leaves of M. dodecandrum, alongside the expression topology of key structural genes involved in their biosynthesis. Metabolomic profiling revealed that flavonoids -predominant flavonols- were significantly enriched in foliar and root tissues. A total of 20 major flavonoids were annotated, among which quercetin-3-O-glucosyl-(1→2)-rhamnoside emerged as the most abundant constituent in both leaves and roots, suggesting its pivotal role in the plant's pharmacological efficacy. Leveraging the published reference genome of M. dodecandrum for transcriptome analysis, we systematically identified key catalytic enzyme genes within the flavonoid biosynthetic pathway, including CHS, CHI, and DFR. Notably, their organ-specific expression patterns highly mirrored the accumulation dynamics of their corresponding metabolites. Furthermore, integrated KEGG pathway enrichment analysis demonstrated that flavonoid-specific metabolic pathways dictate the distinct chemophenotypic differentiation among different organs. In conclusion, this study decodes the molecular mechanism governing the chemical quality formation of M. dodecandrum, establishing a robust theoretical framework for the sustainable development and high-value utilization of this medicinalresource.

papers.title: L-Threonine production from acetate by metabolically engineered Corynebacterium glutamicum using a pH-controlled fed-batch process
papers.abstract: Acetate has a considerable potential as a non-food feedstock for microbial bioproduction, yet its use for amino acid production remains underexplored. Here, we developed a process for L-threonine production from acetate as the sole carbon source with Corynebacterium glutamicum by integrating rational, genome-based metabolic engineering with pH-coupled fed-batch cultivation. The engineered strain AT-3 carried five chromosomal mutations that alleviated feedback inhibition of key enzymes and redirected carbon flux toward the aspartate pathway. Substrate supply was controlled using a custom Visual Basic-based feeding script that automatically adjusted the acetic acid feed in response to online pH measurements. Robust process performance was maintained during a tenfold scale-up from 100-mL DASbox to 1-L DASGIP bioreactors. The optimized process achieved an L-threonine titer of 10.04 g/L and a yield of 0.086 g/g acetate. This study provides a basis for further studies on the development and improvement of acetate-based amino acid production process. KEY POINTS: • Plasmid-free C. glutamicum strains produce L-threonine in acetate minimal medium • pH-controlled acetic acid feed in bioreactors improved L-threonine production • Acetate-based production of feed amino acids avoids competition with human food.

papers.title: Beyond Digestion: The Gastrointestinal Tract at the Centre of Metabolic Regulation
papers.abstract: Traditionally, gastrointestinal (GI) and metabolic disease have been considered separate clinical entities with the GI tract viewed primarily as a conduit for digestion and nutrient absorption, while the metabolic regulation was largely attributed to the liver, pancreas, and adipose tissue. Recent evidence, has challenged this distinction and has demonstrated that the intestine functions as a major endocrine, immune, and metabolic organ playing a key role in metabolic health. The emergence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the success of incretin-based therapies, and the metabolic benefits of bariatric interventions highlight the increasingly interconnected nature of gastrointestinal and metabolic health. In this perspective, we propose a gut–metabolic network framework in which the intestine serves as a central integrator linking the metabolic system together. This framework extends beyond the conventional gut–liver axis and helps explain the multisystem effects of contemporary therapies. We discuss key mechanistic pathways, therapeutic convergence between gastroenterology and metabolic medicine, and important gaps in current clinical practice, including limited metabolic phenotyping and fragmented care models. Recognizing the gut as a central regulator of metabolic health may enable more integrated approaches to patient care, research, and training, and better align clinical practice with evolving biological understanding.

papers.title: Toward climate-resilient date palm agriculture in the United Arab Emirates: a strategic triangulated knowledge mapping
papers.abstract: The date palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.) plays a vital role in food security, rural livelihoods, and cultural heritage in the hyper-arid United Arab Emirates (UAE). However, increasing climate stress, water scarcity, and persistent production constraints threaten the sector’s long-term resilience. Addressing these challenges requires a comprehensive understanding of existing research and its limitations. This study systematically maps the thematic structure of UAE date-palm research, identifies dominant knowledge domains, and highlights critical gaps hindering the transition toward climate-resilient and integrated agricultural systems. A mixed-methods approach was adopted, combining bibliometric analysis of 124 peer-reviewed articles (2005–2026) with Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modelling to identify major thematic clusters. A complementary systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted to validate findings and synthesize emerging research trajectories. The results reveal a mature, internationally collaborative research landscape structured around ten thematic clusters, with Date Palm Diseases and Control and Phytochemical and Nutritional Analysis emerging as dominant motor themes. Despite advances in water management, biomass valorization, and genomics, the field remains fragmented, with limited integration across technological, environmental, and socio-economic dimensions. Significant gaps persist, particularly in IoT and blockchain-enabled agricultural systems and in socio-technical studies of innovation adoption. This study provides an evidence-based roadmap, emphasizing unified socio-technical frameworks to support a sustainable and climate-resilient UAE date-palm sector. Graphical abstract

papers.title: Explainable artificial intelligence for laser powder bed fusion alloys: breaking the formability–performance trade-off via collaborative control
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables the fabrication of metallic components with complex geometries and high performance. However, achieving coordinated control of formability including defect suppression and cracking resistance together with mechanical properties such as strength, ductility, and fatigue life remains a critical challenge for LPBF alloys. Although artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely adopted for process optimization, defect prediction, and performance evaluation, conventional AI models often lack physical metallurgical interpretability, leading to limited generalization and unreliable extrapolation beyond training domains. This review focuses on the role of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) in addressing the formability–performance trade-off in LPBF alloys. We first introduce four knowledge domains that establish physical interpretability in metallic materials: physical metallurgy principles, cross-scale numerical information, microstructure image analysis, and causal physical mechanisms. Subsequently, we systematically examine XAI applications across representative LPBF alloy systems. In performance-oriented alloys such as steels and titanium alloys, XAI facilitates mechanism–aware control of non-equilibrium phase transformations, microstructural anisotropy, and defect-sensitive fatigue behavior. In formability-oriented alloys including aluminum alloys and nickel-based superalloys, XAI supports cracking susceptibility prediction, process–window identification, and printable alloy design. Despite these advances, most current studies remain task-specific and single-objective, with limited integration of formability and performance optimization. To overcome this limitation, we propose a unified multi-objective optimization framework incorporating physically constrained modeling, standardized multimodal databases, and causal reasoning. This review provides guidance for the intelligent, reliable, and collaborative design of LPBF alloys with both high formability and excellent mechanical performance.
papers.summary: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables the fabrication of metallic components with complex geometries and high performance. Despite these advances, most current studies remain task-specific and single-objective, with limited integration of formability and performance optimization. This review provides guidance for the intelligent, reliable, and collaborative design of LPBF alloys with both high formability and excellent mechanical performance.

papers.title: Microencapsulation of okra mucilage: extraction, characterization, and potential application in jaggery processing
papers.abstract: Okra ( Abelmoschus esculentus L.) mucilage is a polysaccharide-rich, natural bioactive compound known for its functional and therapeutic properties. This study aimed to microencapsulate okra mucilage using cassava starch as the wall material and to characterize the microcapsules, with a focus on their application as a natural clarifying agent in the processing of sugarcane juice/jaggery. The freeze-drying technique was used to microencapsulate the mucilage from okra fruit (without peduncle) and peduncle. The mucilage was extracted using three distinct methods: solvent precipitation, grinding-centrifugation-solvent, and ultrasonic-assisted solvent extraction. The ultrasonic-assisted solvent extraction method yielded the highest mucilage recovery of 11.67% for okra fruit and 10.03% for okra peduncle. The encapsulation efficiency reached 61% for fruit and 56% for peduncle. X-ray diffraction showed an enhanced crystallinity, from 33.52% for raw mucilage of okra fruit to 55.23% for the encapsulated fruit sample, and from 29.02% for raw mucilage of okra peduncle to 78.25% for the encapsulated peduncle sample. This improved microcapsule structural order alongside a high glass transition temperature ( Tg = 74.8 °C) verified by differential scanning calorimetry, significantly enhanced the stability of the cassava starch-encapsulated mucilage against thermal stress. This stabilzation enabled effective impurity removal during high-temperature sugarcane juice clarification. FTIR and LC–MS analyses revealed galacturonic acid, mannose, Quercetin-3-O-glucoside, and Rutin (quercetin-3-O-rutinoside) as the primary compounds driving clarification. The incorporation of encapsulated mucilage during jaggery processing significantly improved clarification efficiency by 45% and increased scum removal by 1.45-fold at a 1 g/L dosage compared to the control. Furthermore, the foaming capacity was significantly supressed to 250% and 130%, respectively, with the addition of encapsulated mucilage at concentrations of 1 g/L and 2 g/L, respectively.

papers.title: Can the Spatial Planning of Livestock Production Tackle Future Nitrogen Pollution in China?
papers.abstract: Abstract Nitrogen (N) pollution from livestock production significantly threatens China’s air and water quality, necessitating innovative solutions to balance food security and environmental sustainability. Studies have mostly overlooked the spatial heterogeneity of N-related environmental impacts and the trade-offs between reducing ammonia (NH3) emissions and N concentrations in water. This study develops a spatially explicit multiscale model system encompassing 13,000 polygons across China to assess soil N balance, NH3 emission intensity, and N concentrations in surface water, aiming to explore integrated spatial-planning (SP) strategies that maximize synergy and minimize trade-offs. Our findings reveal that single-purpose SP scenarios (e.g., reducing NH3 emissions or instream N concentrations) can effectively address one N-related issue but produce substantial trade-offs, leaving >50% of China’s population exposed to at least another N-related problem. However, an integrated SP approach could reduce harmful N exposures for 90% of China’s population while ensuring food security. This approach involves reallocating 14% of livestock production, reducing livestock numbers by one-third relative to the 2050 baseline, and implementing advanced technologies to mitigate N pollution hotspots. Thus, our findings emphasize the importance of spatially explicit N boundaries and multicriteria planning to tackle N pollution in air and water simultaneously, supporting cross-media N management policy-making and region-specific strategies.

papers.title: MSER-DDI: molecular and semantic event representations for few-shot and unseen-event drug–drug interaction prediction
papers.abstract: Introduction Sparse event annotations limit drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction, particularly for rare events and event categories absent from training data. Methods We propose MSER-DDI, a framework with two independently trained pathways that represent target events using labeled drug pairs or textual descriptions. The sample-driven pathway, PharDDIE, combines molecular structure and biological context with reconstruction-regularized latent encoding to construct event prototypes from a few labeled pairs. The semantics-driven pathway, EviDDIE, maps event descriptions into the drug-pair representation space and uses evidential inference without labeled target-event examples. Results In 1-shot rare-event prediction, PharDDIE achieved higher mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), accuracy, and event-macro F1 than retrained RareDDIE across five matched training seeds. These means also exceeded the published baseline estimates. Under the respective evaluation conditions, 5-shot predictions had lower Brier score, negative log-likelihood, and calibration error than 1-shot predictions, together with lower high-confidence error rates and broader coverage across all three event-frequency groups. EviDDIE predicted interactions for event categories excluded from molecular training. Literature-based assessment identified drug- or class-level pharmacological consistency for a subset of selected positive benchmark examples. Discussion MSER-DDI supports event-level prediction when target-event annotations are scarce or unavailable, while joint evaluation of discrimination and probability quality characterizes predictive performance and confidence. The resulting predictions provide interaction hypotheses for further pharmacological investigation.

papers.title: Nanobiochar derived from organic waste: a sustainable solution for agriculture, environment, and circular bioeconomy
papers.journal: International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology
papers.abstract: The rapid increase in organic waste generation, water contamination, and soil degradation presents major global environmental challenges. Conventional treatment methods, including activated carbon adsorption, chemical remediation, and bulk biochar application, are effective but often limited by high cost, low selectivity, and reduced efficiency for emerging contaminants. Nanobiochar has recently gained attention as an advanced alternative due to its enhanced physicochemical properties; however, a comprehensive understanding of its production, performance, and large-scale applicability remains limited. This review provides a systematic evaluation of nanobiochar derived from organic waste within the framework of sustainable resource management and circular bioeconomy. It examines production pathways involving pyrolysis followed by size reduction and surface modification techniques, including ball milling, sonication, and chemical treatment, along with key characterization approaches. Nanobiochar demonstrates significantly improved surface area (200–500 m2/g), porosity, and functional groups compared to conventional biochar, leading to enhanced adsorption capacity and reactivity. In wastewater treatment, removal efficiencies exceeding 90–99% have been reported for heavy metals and organic pollutants. In agricultural applications, nanobiochar improves soil fertility, nutrient retention, water holding capacity, microbial activity, and crop yield by 15–40%. Techno-economic analysis indicates that nanobiochar production is cost-effective ($500–1500/ton) and offers lower operational costs compared to conventional adsorbents, while contributing to carbon sequestration and waste valorization. Overall, nanobiochar is a promising multifunctional material; however, further research is required to address scalability, long-term environmental impacts, and regulatory challenges. papers.title: Self-biased magnetoelectric Ni/LiNbO₃/Ni composites: from material characterisation to a battery-free implantable node
papers.journal: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
papers.abstract: Abstract Self-biased magnetoelectric (ME) composites, which convert a magnetic field into electricity with no static bias, are attractive for powering battery-free, deeply implanted microsystems through tissue without heating it, while returning their data. This paper develops a self-biased Ni/LiNbO₃/Ni composite in which sputter-deposited nickel acts both as the magnetostrictive phase and as the electrodes; an intrinsic residual stress (≈ 50 MPa, confirmed by temperature-dependent VSM) supplies the bias and removes the static field, permanent magnets and epoxy bonding of conventional ME laminates. A unified equivalent circuit, a Mason model reduced near resonance to a Butterworth–Van Dyke network closed by a magneto-mechanical gyrator and a piezoelectric transformer, all elements extracted in closed form from impedance and VSM data, predicts the deliverable power within a factor of two across four composites over two decades of output, and is ready for end-to-end co-simulation in SPICE (Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis). Guided by a fill-factor and skin-depth design study, an optimised sample raises the output from ≈ 1 V / 16 µW to 8.5 V / 0.33 mW self-biased (1.5 mW under a small bias). This power is shown, by circuit simulation on the measured source and by a measured-power budget, to run a complete battery-free node: the ME link supplies a pressure sensor, its analogue-to-digital converter and a microcontroller, a 13.56 MHz backscatter channel returns the data, and the harvested power lets a semi-active uplink clear the range limit of passive backscatter at 10 cm. A dosimetric and thermal analysis shows the low operating frequency to be a primary safety enabler (induced field and SAR scale as f and f²): the ME link deposits 50 to 130 times less specific absorption rate than an iso-footprint 13.56 MHz inductive link operated at the field its own standard permits.

papers.title: Attention-Derived Dependency Cut for Independent KV-Cache Reuse in Agent Memory
papers.journal: International Journal of Network Dynamics and Intelligence
papers.abstract: Long-term agent memory grows continuously with interaction, making full-memory prefill increasingly costly in terms of time to first token (TTFT) and redundant computation. KV-cache reuse could avoid repeatedly prefilling the accumulated memory, but KV caching relies on exact prefix matching. When memory is updated, reorganized, or assembled from reusable units, prefix mismatches prevent direct reuse of existing KV caches and force the model to recompute a long memory prefix. Existing methods largely assume that memory blocks are already given and address the prefix-matching limitation by concatenating their KV caches and then repairing the resulting mismatch. We therefore argue that the primary question for agent-memory KV reuse is where to segment the memory. We propose AD-CUT, an Attention-derived dependency Cut method for training-free, independence-oriented segmentation. AD-Cut computes attention-derived dependency signals over sentence-level atomic units, including an incoming signal Ain and an outgoing signal Aout, and selects boundaries where both signals are low. The signals exhibit stable positive associations with intervention-derived KV and NLL sensitivity, with Spearman ρ ranging from 0.615 to 0.868 and context-cluster bootstrap intervals remaining positive, supporting their use as predictive proxies. In block-KV serving for agent QA, AD-Cut achieves a 16.17× Online TTFT speedup with a QA Quality Retention of 0.7675. It also improves task quality over naive sentence-level reuse in a controlled agent-memory evaluation. These results show that AD-Cut substantially reduces online computation while mitigating the quality loss caused by KV-cache reuse.

These results show that AD-Cut substantially reduces online computation while mitigating the quality loss caused by KV-cache reuse.

papers.title: Quantitative Toxicophore Discovery through Interpretable Deep Learning: A Framework for Mechanism-Guided Toxicity Mitigation in Drug Safety Profiling
papers.abstract: Abstract Unanticipated toxicity accounts for ∼30% of clinical-phase drug failures, yet despite advances in computational toxicity prediction, predictive models typically offer scores without identifying the structural culprit. Here, we introduce an interpretable deep-learning framework that couples fingerprint-descriptor fusion with task-adaptive attention and a SHAP-guided bioisosteric ablation pipeline. Trained on 9,315 compounds spanning 14 end points (Tox21 + ClinTox) under scaffold-stratified split, the attention-fusion model achieves mean test ROC-AUC of 0.739 (Tox21) and 0.953 (ClinTox). The critical advance is a structure-guided validation protocol: predictive intervention ablation─computationally replacing toxicophores with bioisosteric equivalents─demonstrates that the model’s predictions are predictively dependent on specific substructures. Halogen → methyl substitution drops predicted toxicity from 0.659 to 0.101 (paired t = 22.66, p = 6.32 × 10–10, n = 11; Cohen’s d = 6.82), providing the primary structure-guided evidence. Cross-end point SHAP correlation reaches 0.333 (MTL) and 0.334 (STL; Welch’s p = 0.82), indicating that both paradigms extract coherent mechanistic structure above the label baseline (0.172). SMARTS-based toxicophore alignment identifies a strong positive logit differential for aniline on the clinically relevant CT_TOX end point (+0.76), and predictive-intervention ablation confirms model dependence on the identified substructures (halogen → methyl: n = 11, p < 10–9; aniline → methoxy: n = 2, directional check only). External validation on 1,427 SIDER adverse-drug-reaction compounds reveals significant toxicophore enrichment (aniline: 12.6% vs 0%, Fisher exact p = 4.5 × 10–12; halogenated aromatic: 29.8% vs 0%, p = 1.6 × 10–29), remaining significant after controlling for molecular weight and Log P. Three case studies illustrate how SHAP-guided attribution translates into actionable medicinal-chemistry mitigation strategies.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals cellular atlases and cell–cell interaction networks in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)
papers.abstract: Objective To summarize recent advances in single-cell multi-omics technologies in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), with a focus on cellular atlases, cellular heterogeneity, and intercellular communication networks in hepatic and extrahepatic tissues. Methods This narrative review synthesizes findings from studies identified primarily through PubMed searches supplemented by manual curation of reference lists. Search terms included “single-cell,” “spatial transcriptomics,” “MASLD,” “NAFLD,” “NASH,” “MASH,” “steatohepatitis,” and “liver fibrosis.” Studies applying single-cell transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, single-cell eQTL analysis, and integrative multi-omics approaches were included. The last literature search was conducted in July 2026. Results: Single-cell technologies have revealed key cellular alterations during MASLD progression, including disrupted hepatocyte metabolic zonation, heterogeneous activation states of hepatic stellate cells, macrophage functional reprogramming, immune cell dysfunction, and dynamic remodeling of the hepatic microenvironment. Spatial transcriptomics has further resolved the spatial organization of these cellular changes, whereas single-cell eQTL analyses have linked genetic susceptibility loci to cell-specific regulatory programs. Single-cell profiling of intestinal, adipose, and vascular tissues has expanded the understanding of extrahepatic contributions and gut–liver communication in MASLD. These advances provide a foundation for drug target identification, mechanistic understanding of current and investigational therapies, and assessment of treatment response at cellular resolution. Conclusion Single-cell multi-omics is transforming MASLD research from tissue-level characterization toward cellular-resolution understanding, providing novel insights into disease stratification, therapeutic target discovery, and biomarker development, and advancing precision hepatology.

papers.title: Electric Field Assisted Through‐Thickness Alignment of Carboxyl Functionalized Graphene in Glass Fiber/Epoxy Laminates: Emphasizing Bending, Interlaminar Shear and Fracture Behavior
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT A possible way to enhance the Z‐directional mechanical characteristics of laminated GFRP composites is by suitable through‐thickness alignment of secondary reinforcements. In this work, efficient alignment of polar carboxyl functionalized graphene (FG) in a laminated GFRP composite has been achieved by optimizing the applied z‐directional A.C. field strength. The laminate AF300, where the field strength is 300 V/mm exhibited the best flexural strength among all the composites considered, which is 17% and 32% higher over randomly oriented FG embedded GFRP (RF) and neat GFRP composites respectively. Dynamic mechanical analysis also suggests similar effect where the storage modulus of AF300 composite was found to be significantly better over both RF and Neat composites. Short beam strength as obtained indicates efficient restriction towards delamination due to the through‐thickness alignment of FG. A substantial improvement in energy absorption during Mode I inter laminar fracture toughness (ILFT) test has been noticed due to alignment of FG in the GFRP composite. Similarly, AF300 composite exhibited 84% better Mode II ILFT over the neat composite. Through thickness electrical conductance of AF300 composite is 350% better than Neat and 80% better then RF composite, indicating successful alignment of FG along through thickness direction.

papers.title: Sheng-Jiang Powder and Akkermansia muciniphila interventions in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis: microbiota-linked sphingolipid/S1PR1-associated barrier remodeling
papers.abstract: Background Sheng-Jiang Powder (SJP) is a classical traditional Chinese medicine formula with reported anti-inflammatory and gut microbiota-modulating activities. However, whether its protective effects in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) are associated with gut microbial changes, sphingolipid/S1P metabolism, and S1PR1-related barrier signaling remains unclear. Methods EAE was induced in female C57BL/6 mice, with SJP, Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK intervention group), or their combination administered from day 2 after immunization, before the expected onset of clinical signs. Clinical severity, histopathology, inflammatory cytokines, and barrier-related markers were evaluated. Gut microbiota changes were assessed by fluorescence in situ hybridization and 16S rRNA sequencing. Untargeted serum and fecal metabolomic profiles were analyzed by LC–MS. Serum-detected SJP-related compounds were characterized by UPLC–MS/MS and analyzed using network pharmacology. S1PR1-associated signaling was further examined by Western blotting, immunofluorescence, and S1PR1-overexpression experiments in bEnd.3 cells. Results Pre-onset SJP, AKK, and AKK_SJP interventions reduced EAE severity, inflammatory pathology, and serum inflammatory cytokine levels. These effects were accompanied by improved colonic barrier markers, increased Akkermansia -associated mucosal signals, and altered gut microbial profiles. Serum and fecal metabolomic analyses highlighted lipid-related pathways, particularly sphingolipid metabolism and signaling. Serum-detected SJP-related compounds mapped to a candidate network containing S1PR1. In colon and CNS tissues, treatment altered barrier-related markers and S1PR1 expression. In bEnd.3 cells, S1PR1 overexpression reduced ZO-1 expression, whereas SJP-containing serum partially attenuated this change. Conclusions Pre-onset SJP administration alleviated EAE and was accompanied by changes in gut microbial composition, sphingolipid/S1P-related metabolism, S1PR1 expression, and barrier-related markers. AKK-related intervention showed overlapping effects on several microbial, metabolic, and barrier-associated markers.
