The experimental results showed that the maximum compressive modulus of the LMCP/SA/CNF aerogel was 6.57 MPa, and the compressive stress was 1.313 MPa. In summary, the development of this innovative antibacterial aerogel material demonstrates its application potential as a packaging cushioning material, providing new technical insights for this field.

papers.title: Objective assessment and virtual lesion simulation of psoriasis lesion severity based on deep learning regression and generative models
papers.abstract: Objective The Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) remains the gold standard for evaluating psoriasis severity; however, the assessment of its subscores—erythema, scaling, and induration—relies heavily on clinicians’ subjective judgment, leading to poor inter-rater consistency. This study aims to develop an objective evaluation model, Psoriasis-RegNet, based on deep learning regression, using publicly available dermatological image repositories, and to explore a conditional generative model, Psoriasis-GAN, for creating virtual lesion simulations of psoriasis lesions and demonstrating their potential applications in medical education. Methods A total of 1,250 clinical images of psoriasis were collected from the public DermNet dermatology image archive. Based on the accompanying clinical descriptions, a large pre-trained language-vision model was employed to automatically annotate each image with erythema ( E ), scaling ( S ), and induration ( I ) scores on a 0–4 scale, thereby constructing a multi-label regression dataset. The reliability of the pseudo-labels was evaluated against independent annotations from board-certified dermatologists, yielding ICC values of 0.86, 0.83, and 0.79 for erythema, scaling, and induration, respectively. (1) Psoriasis-RegNet: We developed a multi-task regression network using ResNet-50 as the backbone, pretrained on the ISIC 2019 skin lesion dataset. Three independent regression heads were attached to predict the E , S , and I scores, respectively, enabling simultaneous quantitative evaluation of lesion severity components. (2) Psoriasis-GAN: We further implemented a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) based on the StyleGAN2-ADA architecture. The composite vector E,S,I was used as the conditional input to guide the generation of high-resolution psoriasis lesion images, supporting controllable and clinically meaningful visual synthesis. Results The Psoriasis-RegNet model demonstrated excellent performance on the held-out internal test set. The mean absolute errors (MAE) for erythema, scaling, and induration predictions were 0.42, 0.45, and 0.48, respectively. The Pearson correlation coefficients (PCC) between model predictions and the held-out reference labels were 0.85, 0.82, and 0.80 for erythema, scaling, and induration, respectively (all P < 0.001). These prediction errors are within the range of inter-rater variability reported among dermatologists for PASI subscores (typical MAE: 0.5–0.9). The Psoriasis-GAN successfully generated high-fidelity (1,024 × 1,024) and conditionally controllable lesion images, achieving a Frechet Inception Distance (FID) of 28.5, and a Visual Turing Test discrimination accuracy of 51.3 percent, indicating near-photorealistic quality. Conclusion This study demonstrates that re-annotation of public dermatological image repositories provides a feasible approach for developing AI models in dermatology. The proposed Psoriasis-RegNet offers an objective and quantitative tool for psoriasis severity assessment, while Psoriasis-GAN shows great potential for medical education and AI data augmentation through the creation of virtual lesion simulations that enable interactive exploration of psoriasis severity phenotypes.
papers.summary: This study aims to develop an objective evaluation model, Psoriasis-RegNet, based on deep learning regression, using publicly available dermatological image repositories, and to explore a conditional generative model, Psoriasis-GAN, for creating virtual lesion simulations of psoriasis lesions and demonstrating their potential applications in medical education. Results The Psoriasis-RegNet model demonstrated excellent performance on the held-out internal test set. Conclusion This study demonstrates that re-annotation of public dermatological image repositories provides a feasible approach for developing AI models in dermatology.

papers.title: Comparative shotgun metagenomic analysis of the feline fecal microbiome in response to fresh, dry, and wet diets in a randomized crossover trial
papers.abstract: Fresh (mildly cooked) cat foods are an increasingly popular alternative to conventional extruded dry and retorted wet diets, differing in their processing and formulation. While the gut microbiota play an important role in feline health and physiological functions, characterization of the gut microbiome in cats fed fresh diets and direct comparisons with dry and wet diets have not yet been performed. In this 42-day, 3 × 3 Latin square crossover trial, 15 healthy adult cats received commercial, chicken-based, complete fresh, dry, and wet diets in one of three randomized diet sequences. Each diet was fed for 14 days, with fecal samples collected on days 12–14 for shotgun metagenomic sequencing, followed by taxonomic and functional annotation. Shannon and Simpson indices were lower with the dry diet than with the other two diets ( p < 0.001 for fresh vs. dry, p < 0.01 for wet vs. dry for both indices), while Chao1 was higher for the wet diet than for the dry ( p < 0.05) and fresh diets ( p < 0.001). PERMANOVA using Bray-Curtis distances showed significant differences in species, pathway, and CAZy term compositions among diets (all p < 0.001). The five most abundant phyla with the fresh and wet diets were Bacteroidota, Bacillota_A, Actinomycetota, Pseudomonadota, and Bacillota, whereas Bacillota_C replaced Pseudomonadota when cats were fed the dry diet. Differential abundance analysis of taxonomic and functional data using MaAsLin2 identified diet-associated changes (FDR-adjusted p < 0.10). Collinsella, Bacteroides , and Blautia species were enriched and Prevotella species were depleted with the fresh compared with the dry diet, while Prevotella species were depleted with the fresh compared with the wet diet. The dry diet was associated with amino acid biosynthesis, bacterial cell envelope biosynthesis, and polysaccharide degradation; the fresh diet with amino acid degradation, lipid biosynthesis, and utilization of starch/glycogen, fructans, and host-associated glycans; and the wet diet shared functional similarities with the other two diets. The current study demonstrates differences in the feline fecal microbiome at the species level and in predicted functional profiles among fresh, dry, and wet diets, however health implications remain unclear before they can inform feeding recommendations.

PERMANOVA using Bray-Curtis distances showed significant differences in species, pathway, and CAZy term compositions among diets (all p < 0.001). The current study demonstrates differences in the feline fecal microbiome at the species level and in predicted functional profiles among fresh, dry, and wet diets, however health implications remain unclear before they can inform feeding recommendations.

papers.title: A Review of Methylglyoxal Content and Antioxidant Potential of Apis cerana and Apis dorsata Honey from Sumbawa for Functional Livestock Products and Veterinary Health
papers.abstract: Honey produced by Apis cerana and Apis dorsata in Sumbawa, Indonesia, is widely recognized for its medicinal value, primarily due to its rich content of methylglyoxal (MGO), phenolic compounds, and flavonoids. These bioactive components contribute to the honey’s strong antioxidant and antibacterial properties, offering potential benefits for improving livestock health. This review explores the MGO concentration and antioxidant activity of both A. cerana and A. dorsata honey from Sumbawa, while assessing its potential as a functional livestock supplement within the One Health approach. Relevant literature from 2004 to 2025 was systematically reviewed using Scopus, PubMed, and Google Scholar databases. Honey from managed colonies (A. cerana) and wild nests (A. dorsata) was typically analyzed using HPLC, SERS, or qNMR for MGO quantification, while antioxidant potential was measured through Folin-Ciocalteu, aluminum chloride, DPPH, and FRAP assays. Findings indicate that A. cerana honey shows varying MGO levels influenced by floral sources and location, while studies on A. dorsata honey remain limited. Both types demonstrate significant antioxidant activity linked to their phenolic and flavonoid content. Evidence suggests their role in reducing oxidative stress, supporting immune function, and promoting livestock well-being. Overall, Sumbawa honey, especially from A. cerana, shows promise as a natural additive for livestock health management, aligning with sustainable agriculture and One Health principles. Further in vivo research is required to validate its therapeutic potential, particularly for A. dorsata honey.

papers.title: Secular trends and pubertal growth spurts in body height among Tibetan children and adolescents living at high altitudes in Lhasa (China) from 1965 to 2019
papers.abstract: Abstract Height is an anthropometric measure of nutritional levels and health status during childhood and adolescence and can strongly predict health and developmental outcomes across the lifespan. There is little evidence on the growth trends of Chinese children and adolescents living at high altitudes. This paper aimed to examine the secular trends and pubertal growth spurts in height among Tibetan children and adolescents in Lhasa from 1965 to 2019. Height data among Tibetan children and adolescents aged 7–17 years were obtained from ten cross-sectional surveys (1965, 1975, 1985, 1991, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2014, and 2019). Sample-weighted regressions (linear or quadratic or cubic regressions) were performed to estimate trends in height by sex and age. A population-weighting procedure was used to calculate the changes for boys and girls. The SuperImposition by Translation and Rotation model was used to separately fit height–distance and height–velocity curves for boys and girls, yielding sex- and wave-specific peak height velocity (PHV) and age at PHV (APHV). The results showed that population-based height increased by 17.8 cm or 2.28 effect size (ES) for boys and by 14.1 cm or 1.98 ES for girls from 1965 to 2019. Among boys, there was a moderate increase per decade (0.76 ES) from 1965 to 1970, followed by a gradual deceleration in this trend. For girls, there was a largest increase per decade (0.74 ES) in 1960s. Then, the trend slowed and remained stable in the last decades. From 1965 to 2019, the PHV for boys increased from 6.53 cm/year to 7.36 cm/year ( P = 0.007), whereas the APHV decreased from 15.84 years to 13.39 years ( P < 0.001). Girls showed no significant trend in PHV, but APHV decreased from 12.85 years to 10.00 years. In sum, this study reveals a secular trend in height among Tibetan children and adolescents in Lhasa over the past five decades, with a recent deceleration in trends. Puberty development has advanced in both sexes. More public health policies are needed to promote the growth and development of Tibetan children and adolescents and prevent negative impacts from sustained growth and early puberty.

The results showed that population-based height increased by 17.8 cm or 2.28 effect size (ES) for boys and by 14.1 cm or 1.98 ES for girls from 1965 to 2019. More public health policies are needed to promote the growth and development of Tibetan children and adolescents and prevent negative impacts from sustained growth and early puberty.

papers.title: Leakage-resistant graph learning for risk propagation and risk-constrained control in construction supply networks
papers.abstract: Introduction Construction supply network decisions require both predecision warning from information available before operations unfold and topology-aware diagnosis after the disruption context becomes visible. We introduce an auditable framework that separates these regimes through a strict start-of-week information contract and connects risk scores to safety-gated resource allocation. Methods We combined public SUCCESS construction-logistics records with a frozen queue-flow mechanism producing paired counterfactual outcomes on a heterogeneous network with 302 nodes and 1,277 edges. Models were trained on pilots A and B, selected on pilot C, and evaluated on pilot D. The strict contract excluded all week-t outcomes, service levels, and shock-source indicators. Complementary evaluations comprised context-aware diagnosis, a construction consolidation center (CCC) outage panel, leave-one-project-out evaluation, and an independent SupplyGraph boundary test. Six resource policies were compared through validation-only selection and a held-out Pareto audit. Results Under the strict contract, the graph convolutional network achieved the highest held-out area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.2397 and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.8161 for 4,252 node-weeks with 60 positives. In the context-aware regime, relational GraphSAGE achieved an AUPRC of 0.5702, exceeding the matched multilayer perceptron (MLP) by 0.0803. Across eight positive pairs involving CCC outages, GraphSAGE achieved an AUPRC of 0.5845 versus 0.4994 for the MLP, with a positive pair-specific advantage in each case. The calibrated-risk guardrail identified an aggregate service improvement of 0.827% but screened the allocation out because the affected sites and failure durations increased. The held-out frontier also identified a deficit-only allocation that improved unserved demand, affected sites, and failure durations without overriding the predeclared deployment rule. Discussion The framework combines leakage-resistant graph evaluation, context-aware relational diagnosis, project-level applicability testing, and risk-gated network control. Its explicit safety gate prevents aggregate efficiency gains from concealing propagation-risk transfer.

papers.title: Thermomechanical properties and high-temperature stability of epoxy resin modified with boron-based inorganic phases
papers.journal: Journal of Thermal Analysis and Calorimetry
papers.abstract: Abstract This study concerns the manufacturing and complex characterization of the Epidian 5 epoxy resin with the addition of low-density ceramic phases, containing boron in their crystallographic structure. The composite was designed to contain fine powders of boron carbide and hexagonal boron nitride in quantities up to 20 vol% as reference compositions, compared with a material prepared with up to 20 vol% of a 50/50 vol% mixture of boron carbide and boron nitride. Low additive contents caused a slight decrease in the glass transition temperature, whereas significant changes in storage modulus were observed at inorganic phase concentrations of 10 vol% and above. The incorporation of boron-based phases generally resulted in nearly linear changes in thermal transport properties and hardness. Hexagonal boron nitride exerted the strongest effect on thermal diffusivity and thermal conductivity, while boron carbide produced the most pronounced increase in hardness. Composites containing the BCBN mixture exhibited intermediate thermal and mechanical properties, particularly at higher inorganic phase concentrations. The paper explains material’s behavior through thermal analysis, dynamic mechanical analysis, dilatometry and heat transfer, and the correlations among them. Due to the wide range of potential applications, including military, electrical and coating technologies, the paper characterizes and analyzes the influence of boron-based phases and their mixtures of friction coefficient and material wear.

papers.title: Epidemiological patterns and surveillance-based forecasting of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome in Jiangsu Province, China, 2015–2025
papers.abstract: Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne infectious disease with marked seasonality and geographic heterogeneity. Long-term public health surveillance and independently validated forecasting may help translate routine case reporting into targeted prevention and preparedness. Methods We analysed clinically diagnosed and laboratory-confirmed SFTS cases reported in Jiangsu Province, China, from January 2015 to December 2025. Demographic, occupational, temporal, and county/district-level spatial patterns were described, and local spatial autocorrelation was assessed. Monthly case counts from 2015 to 2023 were used for model development, while 2024–2025 data were reserved for independent temporal testing. Seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), random forest (RF), long short-term memory (LSTM), and weighted ensemble (WE) models were compared using root mean squared error (RMSE), mean squared error (MSE), and mean absolute error (MAE). Results Among 1,660 reported cases, 1,508 (90.8%) occurred in persons aged ≥50 years and 1,042 (62.8%) among farmers. Annual cases increased from 30 in 2015 to 428 in 2024 and 345 in 2025. Overall, 97.6% of cases occurred from April to October, and high-burden areas and high-high spatial clusters were concentrated in southwestern Jiangsu. In the independent testing period, ARIMA achieved the lowest errors (RMSE 15.31, MSE 234.23, MAE 9.70), followed closely by WE (RMSE 16.25, MSE 264.13, MAE 10.50), whereas RF and LSTM showed larger errors. Refit to the complete series, ARIMA projected recurrent warm-season increases in 2026–2027, with uncertainty widening over the forecast horizon. Conclusion SFTS in Jiangsu showed a clear person–place–time pattern that can inform targeted public health action. The best overall out-of-sample performance of a parsimonious ARIMA model demonstrates that routine surveillance data can support practical seasonal forecasting when richer environmental or entomological data streams are unavailable. Forecasts should be updated regularly and used alongside routine epidemiological assessment.
papers.summary: Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne infectious disease with marked seasonality and geographic heterogeneity. Conclusion SFTS in Jiangsu showed a clear person–place–time pattern that can inform targeted public health action. The best overall out-of-sample performance of a parsimonious ARIMA model demonstrates that routine surveillance data can support practical seasonal forecasting when richer environmental or entomological data streams are unavailable.

papers.title: Development of fresh fruit coating based on banana peel pectin with Pickering emulsion of cellulose nanocrystals/Javanese turmeric essential oil for snake fruit preservation
papers.abstract: Snake fruit ( Salacca zalacca var. Pondoh) is susceptible to postharvest deterioration caused by respiration, transpiration, and spoilage fungi. This study developed a banana peel pectin (P)-based coating incorporating a cellulose nanocrystal (CNC)-stabilized Pickering emulsion of Javanese turmeric essential oil (TEO) as an alternative coating for snake fruit preservation. Three coating-forming formulations, namely pectin (P), P/Tween/TEO, and P/CNC/TEO, were evaluated using uncoated fruit as the control, with the fruit tip immersed in the coating solution for 1 min. The selected formulation contained 0.5% P, 0.5% TEO, and 0.05% CNC. Transmission electron microscopy analysis revealed rod-like or needle-like nanoscale morphology of CNC, while gas chromatography–mass spectrometry showed that TEO was dominated by α-curcumene and β-curcumene . Incorporation of 0.05% CNC produced a coating solution with greater electrostatic stability and stronger antifungal activity than the conventional Tween 80-stabilized emulsion. The P/CNC/TEO showed the most negative zeta potential (−83.37 ± 0.55 mV) and the strongest in vitro antifungal activity against Botrytis cinerea and Penicillium digitatum , with inhibition values of 87.37 and 72.53%, respectively. During fruit storage, P/CNC/TEO maintained delayed peel darkening, as indicated by a significantly higher peel L* value on day 7, whereas a* and b* values were not significantly affected. The coating did not significantly affect weight loss, total soluble solids, or pH. These results indicated that CNC-stabilized TEO Pickering emulsions enhanced the in vitro antifungal activity of pectin coatings and helped delay peel darkening of snake fruit.

papers.title: A marine‑derived fibrinolytic protease from Bacillus paramycoides AL6: Partial purification, preliminary characterization and in vivo antithrombotic efficacy
papers.abstract: Thrombosis is a pathological condition characterized by blood clot formation that obstructs blood flow and contributes substantially to morbidity and mortality worldwide.Limitations of conventional thrombolytic therapies have prompted the development of enzyme-based alternatives, particularly microbial fibrinolytic enzymes.The present study aimed to identify the AL6 bacterial isolate, partially purify and preliminarily characterize its fibrinolytic protease and evaluate its antithrombotic efficacy in vivo.Molecular identification using the 16S rRNA gene revealed that the AL6 isolate shared 98.27% similarity with Bacillus paramycoides.The enzyme preparation was subjected to anion-exchange chromatography, yielding a partially purified fibrinolytic enzyme preparation with protein bands in the 30-50 kDa range on SDS-PAGE.In vitro fibrinolytic activity, assessed by clot lysis, increased with increasing enzyme volume, with clot lysis values of 47.02±3.00,57.00±3.67 and 76.30±3.17%at enzyme volumes of 100, 200 and 300 µl, respectively.However, they remained lower than those of streptokinase (81.25-92.31%).In vivo antithrombotic efficacy was evaluated using a κ-carrageenan-induced mouse tail thrombus model, in which the partially purified enzyme markedly reduced thrombus length compared with the negative control and exhibited a dose-dependent effect.The highest thrombus reduction (52.54%) was achieved at 0.88 mg/kg body weight and was not markedly different from the positive control.Preliminary safety assessment showed that bleeding time remained within normal limits, suggesting no apparent alteration in hemostasis under the tested conditions.Overall, the partially purified fibrinolytic protease preparation from B. paramycoides AL6 demonstrated promising in vitro fibrinolytic activity and in vivo antithrombotic efficacy.However, further purification, biochemical characterization and comprehensive safety evaluation are required to determine its potential for future therapeutic development.

papers.title: Data-driven fandom culture: exploring parasocial interactions between digital fan labor and traffic stars using interaction ritual chains theory
papers.abstract: Traffic stars and digital fan labor become a widespread phenomenon in China. Digital fan labor refers to the use of tools and data-driven social media strategies to interact with their favorite stars, organize events, measure popularity, and influence the popularity; such stars are referred to as traffic stars. While existing research has largely focused on the characteristics and motivations of digital fan labor in participating in fan activities, few studies have examined the factors influencing their interactive rituals with other fans and parasocial interactions with their celebrities. Parasocial interactions between traffic stars and digital fan labor refer to fans establishing emotional connections with celebrities through participation in fan activities, while celebrities, in turn, strengthen fan engagement through actions such as commenting and liking posts. At this point, Interaction Ritual Chains Theory provides a theoretical framework for the assessment of the importance of collective effervescence and the shared emotional intensity experienced during group rituals in virtual spaces. Therefore, this study uses factors drawn from interaction ritual chains theory to explore the parasocial interaction between so-called ‘traffic stars’ and the digital fan labor they attract within data-driven fandom communities. The sampling strategy was using snowball sampling of a purposive group, and 329 Chinese fans aged between 18 and 42 years old were selected. SPSS version 26.0 was used to obtain descriptive statistics, t-test, mediation effects and moderation effects, and AMOS version 24.0 was used to investigate the result of correlation analysis. The resulting indicated that virtual experience, sense of community, mutual focus of attention, and shared mood all are all associated to the interactive ritual of digital fan labor. This study also found that interactive ritual outcomes play a mediating role between interactive ritual elements and parasocial interactions, especially having different mediating effects with subgroups. However, personal norms did not have a moderating role regarding ritual ingredients affecting interactive ritual outcomes and parasocial interaction. Consequently, this study identified a noteworthy phenomenon: the parasocial interaction between traffic stars and digital fan labor involving a higher level of interactive rituals arises from a hybrid pattern of online actions that develops in a particular environment.

papers.title: MVCNN model for pediatric obstructive sleep apnea prediction via facial photos
papers.abstract: Introduction Polysomnography (PSG) is the gold standard for pediatric obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) diagnosis but is limited for large-scale screening and telemedicine by high costs and specialized requirements. Given the close correlation between craniofacial features and OSA, this study developed a non-invasive risk stratification model (non-OSA, mild OSA, and moderate-to-severe OSA) using two-dimensional multi-view facial photographs based on a Multi-View Convolutional Neural Network (MVCNN). Materials and methods This multicenter retrospective study included 212 children with frontal and lateral facial photographs linked to polysomnography. Models were evaluated at the patient level after aggregating each participant's available image records. The MVCNN was internally evaluated in 149 patients and externally evaluated in 63 patients. Patient-level discrimination and classification metrics were estimated with bootstrap confidence intervals, and paired bootstrap analysis compared models evaluated on common patients. Results In the internal patient-level evaluation, MVCNN achieved a macro-AUC of 0.898 (95% CI, 0.863-0.930), macro-F1 of 0.839, balanced accuracy of 0.840, and overall accuracy of 0.846. Its macro-AUC exceeded those of ResNet-50 by 0.061 (95% CI, 0.022-0.106; P = 0.004) and VGG-16 by 0.104 (95% CI, 0.057-0.164; P < 0.001). In the external cohort, MVCNN achieved a macro-AUC of 0.876 (95% CI, 0.827-0.919), macro-F1 of 0.833, balanced accuracy of 0.826, and overall accuracy of 0.841. Conclusions Patient-level analyses support the discriminatory performance of multi-view facial photography for pediatric OSA risk stratification in the studied dental cohorts. Prospective validation, direct view-ablation studies, and calibration in broader clinical populations are required before clinical deployment.

papers.title: Fabrication of silk fibroin microspheres via microfluidics for Co-delivery of dexamethasone and epidermal growth factor to promote skin wound healing
papers.abstract: Background The skin, serving as the outermost barrier of the human body, is highly susceptible to injury. Wound healing is a complex biological process, and the widely used repair methodssuch as split-thickness autografts have notable drawbacks. Hence, the development of advanced biomaterials that integrate both safety and multifunctionality for skin wound repair holds significant clinical promise. Methods In this study, silk protein (SF) droplets were prepared using microfluidic technology and cross-linked with ultraviolet light to form microspheres loaded with dexamethasone (Dex) and epidermal growth factor (EGF). The fabricated microspheres were subjected to thorough material characterization. In vitro cellular experiment and in vivo animal experiment were performed to explore the anti-inflammatory properties and wound healing efficacy of the microspheres. Results Characterization via scanning electron microscopy and inverted microscopy revealed that microspheres were uniform, loosely structured, and porous, and exhibited strong liquid absorption capacity. Thermogravimetric analysis, X-ray diffraction, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy results indicated that the material was stable and that the modification was successful. Based on the drug loading, encapsulation efficiency, and in vitro release profiles obtained during formulation optimization, 10 μg/mL EGF and 0.8 mg/mL Dex were selected for the preparation of DESF microspheres used in subsequent biological experiments (DESF microspheres, prepared by first loading EGF into SF microspheres followed by Dex post-loading). CCK-8, live/dead cell staining, and scratch assays confirmed that microspheres are non-toxic and promote cell motility. Angiogenesis experiments showed that the experimental group outperformed the control group in terms of total length, number of branching points and nodes. ELISA indicated that levels of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 were significantly reduced, suggesting that the microspheres exhibit good anti-inflammatory effects. In animal experiments, the wound healing rate in the DESF group reached 95.4% ± 3.7%. Histological and immunofluorescence analyses confirmed that DESF microspheres upregulate the expression of VEGF and CD31, downregulate TNF-α, and upregulate IL-10, thereby suppressing early-stage inflammation, promoting angiogenesis, and accelerating wound repair. Conclusion These findings suggest that the DESF microspheres can promot wound healing, with good biocompatibility, anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic properties. Thus, the DESF microspheres hold considerable promise for skin wound repair.

ELISA indicated that levels of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 were significantly reduced, suggesting that the microspheres exhibit good anti-inflammatory effects.

papers.title: Thermophysical properties and thermal cycling behaviour of RT54 HC nanocomposite phase change materials containing samarium oxide
papers.abstract: This study examines the effects of Sm 2 O 3 content on the thermophysical properties and thermal cycling behaviour of RT54 HC phase change composites. Formulations containing 5–20 wt% Sm 2 O 3 were prepared using vacuum assisted melting, magnetic stirring, and bath sonication. Structural and morphological analyses were combined with calorimetric, thermal conductivity, and thermogravimetric measurements. Samples underwent up to 10,000 melting and solidification cycles between 35 and 75 °C. The characteristic RT54 HC spectral and diffraction features remained observable after nanoparticle incorporation, while the phase change temperature range was largely retained across the formulations. Thermal conductivity measured on compacted powders at 25 °C increased from 0.186 W/(m·K) for pristine RT54 HC to 0.282 W/(m·K) at 20 wt% Sm 2 O 3 , corresponding to a 51.6% enhancement. At 70 °C, the corresponding conductivities with the PCM matrix in the molten state were 0.178 and 0.260 W/(m·K), giving a 46.1% enhancement. The highest first cycle mean liquid region C p , evaluated over 62–75 °C, was 4.64 J/(g·K) at 12.5 wt% Sm 2 O 3 , representing a 75.6% increase. For this formulation, the melting and solidification enthalpies changed from 181 to 180 J/g initially to 165 and 165 J/g after 10,000 cycles, while the mean liquid region C p decreased to 3.28 J/(g·K). Thermogravimetric measurements characterized degradation during programmed heating under nitrogen. The results identify different compositions for maximum thermal conductivity and C p , together with changes in storage capacity during cycling. These findings provide a material characterization basis for subsequent evaluation in thermal energy storage systems.

The results identify different compositions for maximum thermal conductivity and C p , together with changes in storage capacity during cycling.

papers.title: EFFECT OF FATTY ACID CONCENTRATION IN THE WORKING FLUID OF MACHINE HYDRAULIC DRIVES ON BOUNDARY LUBRICATING FILM FORMATION
papers.abstract: An analysis of research regarding the effect of fatty acid additives on enhancing the anti-wear properties of working fluids was conducted. The characteristics and molecular state of the additive within the oil were identified as factors influencing the formation of a boundary lubricating film on friction surfaces. A method for intensifying additive adsorption by subjecting the working fluid to an electric field was proposed. A methodology was developed to experimentally investigate how the concentration of surfactant molecules – specifically the fatty acids under study – affects the formation of a lubricating layer on the friction surfaces of machinery hydraulic drives. Experimental studies were carried out to examine the effect of stearic and oleic acid concentrations on changes in boundary lubricating film thickness when the working fluid undergoes electrostatic treatment. A non-linear relationship between lubricating film thickness and additive concentration was established, and the optimal concentrations of stearic and oleic acids – yielding the maximum boundary lubricating film thickness – were determined.

papers.title: Influence of solvent extraction on phenolic profile using (HPLC–PDA), antioxidant activity, and nutritional values of Grewia tenax (Forssk.) Fiori fruits
papers.abstract: Background Grewia tenax (Forssk.) Fiori is a wild fruit traditionally consumed in arid regions and recognized for its potential nutritional and therapeutic value. This study compares the phenolic composition and antioxidant properties of G. tenax fruit extracts obtained using methanol, ethanol, and water to evaluate their benefits to human nutrition. Methodology Whole fruits were extracted with the three solvents, and phenolic acids and antioxidant activities were analyzed using standard in vitro assays, including 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH), reducing power, and β-carotene bleaching tests. The total phenolic content (TPC) of the G. tenax fruit extracts was determined colorimetrically using the Folin–Ciocalteu method, while free phenolic acids were analyzed by HPLC-PDA. DPPH free radical scavenging activity was assessed by taking 3 mL of sample solutions and mixing different concentrates with each. New stocks of radical solutions were prepared every day. The reduction in absorbance of the resulting solution was observed for 10 min at 515 nm with a spectrophotometer. Results Methanol extracts contained the highest total phenolic content and six distinct phenolic acids, similar to ethanol, while water contained two. Gallic acid was dominant at 917.5, 136.5, and 188.2 μg/g in methanol, ethanol, and water extracts, respectively. DPPH scavenging activity followed the order L-ascorbic acid (89.01) > methanol (59.11) > ethanol (55.07) > water (52.14). Reducing power values were 2.79, 2.11, and 1.77, respectively, and β-carotene assays were positive for all extracts but lower than TBHQ. Conclusion The antioxidant efficiency ranked methanol > ethanol > water. In conclusion, these in vitro findings demonstrate that G. tenax fruit extracts possess strong in vitro antioxidant potential and high phenolic contents. While these chemical characteristics suggest prospective value for functional food development, dedicated in vivo and clinical research will be essential to verify any direct potential human health benefits.

papers.title: Continuous harvesting of intermittent and continuous heats by a mixed ion/electron thermoelectric generator using an ionogel blended with carbon nanotubes
papers.abstract: Abstract Ionic thermoelectric (TE) materials have drawn considerable interest because their thermopower can far exceed that of conventional electronic TE materials. They are typically implemented in ionic thermoelectric capacitors (ITECs) for heat harvesting. However, ITECs can harvest only intermittent heat, and there is no electricity generation under steady temperature. Here, we demonstrate a mixed ion/electron thermoelectric generator (MTEG) that can continuously harvest both intermittent and continuous heats into electricity. The active layer is an ionogel blended with single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNTs), forming a mixed conductor in which the ionic liquid enables ion transport while the SWNT network provides electronically conductive pathways. Under a constant temperature gradient, the MTEG delivers a stable output voltage to an external load, closely resembling the behavior of conventional thermoelectric generators. The thermopower exceeds 11.3 mV·K − 1 , which is 1–2 orders of magnitude higher than the Seebeck coefficient of the best electronic TE materials. This operation is attributed to synergistic effects: hole tunneling across the SWNT network coupled with the large ionic thermopower arising from the Soret effect.

papers.title: The Off-Diagonal Low Rank Property: New Opportunities for Low-Scaling Computational Chemistry Methods
papers.abstract: Many matrices in computational chemistry are neither sparse nor low-rank, making the design of low-scaling algorithms difficult. In this Perspective, we point out that many important matrices in computational chemistry, such as the Coulomb matrix, the electronic repulsion integral tensor, the density matrix, the localized molecular orbital (LMO) coefficient matrix, the Fock matrix, and the nuclear Hessian matrix share the same property: when their basis functions are suitably ordered, their off-diagonal blocks have low numerical ranks (despite that they as a whole have high numerical ranks). This property, termed off-diagonal low rank (ODLR), has been extensively studied in the mathematics community, but has surprisingly found very little use in computational chemistry. This Perspective reviews the existing mathematical literature on how to use the ODLR property of matrices to compactly store, as well as efficiently calculate or use them. Subsequently, we review the use of the ODLR property in computational chemistry, and point out possible future opportunities of devising new low-scaling methods for dense, full-rank matrices, exploiting the ODLR property. In particular, we prove for the first time that Fock matrices and LMO coefficient matrices satisfy the ODLR property, even if the system is gapless (in which case the matrices are dense). This paves the way to linear scaling electronic structure calculations of gapless systems at zero electronic temperature.

papers.title: Antibacterial-Enhanced Benzoxazine-Functionalized ZnO Nanoparticles for Anticorrosion Sol–Gel Coatings
papers.abstract: Abstract In this paper, benzoxazine-functionalized silane (BzPTES) was grafted onto zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) to afford antibacterial-enhanced and dispersible functionalized nanoparticles (ZnO-Bz), which were subsequently incorporated into a sol–gel coating system to construct a dual-functional composite coating with excellent corrosion resistance and antibacterial properties. The structure and dispersion of ZnO-Bz were characterized by FTIR, zeta potential, TGA, and elemental analysis. Coatings’ performance was evaluated by EIS, salt spray test, water contact angle, water absorption tests, plate counting method, and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC). Results show that Bz functional groups were successfully grafted onto ZnO with a grafting ratio of approximately 2.59 wt %. After 30 days of immersion in 3.5 wt % NaCl, the coating with 1 wt % ZnO-Bz maintained a charge transfer resistance exceeding 10 GΩ·cm2, demonstrating the best corrosion resistance. Antibacterial tests showed that the MIC of ZnO-Bz against E. coli and S. aureus was 39 μg/mL, markedly lower than that of unmodified ZnO NPs (39 μg/mL and 156 μg/mL). All coatings containing ZnO-Bz achieved a 100% antibacterial rate against both strains, while the unmodified coating showed rates of only 64.08% and 75.09%, respectively. Incorporating an appropriate amount of ZnO-Bz via a matrix-compatible modification strategy provides an effective approach for developing multifunctional coatings combining corrosion resistance and antibacterial functions.

papers.title: Symmetry in Thermal Fluid Sciences and Energy Applications
papers.abstract: Symmetry is a fundamental notion in thermal-fluid sciences and energy applications and an important tool for understanding the properties of complex systems. Thermal and fluid processes are applied in several modern energy use technologies, basically consisting of the complex multidimensional interaction of fluid mechanics and thermodynamics. A comprehensive analysis involves vector and scalar quantities in the flow field, where symmetry is highly considered in order to simplify geometric parameters. These requirements therefore are also applied to experimental techniques, and the interconnection between experimental analysis and numerical simulation of processes is an important field. Thus, there is a wide range of symmetry solutions for this research area, the results of which contribute to the development of science and fast information for decision-making in industry.

papers.title: Experimental Simulation of Icing-Delay Capability of Asphalt Pavements Made with Wood Sawdust as an Environmentally Friendly Solution
papers.journal: Journal of Materials in Civil Engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract Snow and ice accumulation on asphalt pavements constitute a critical risk to traffic safety, particularly on bridge decks and elevated structures that are highly susceptible to rapid heat loss and premature icing. This study investigated the feasibility of utilizing raw wood sawdust as a partial mineral aggregate replacement in hot-mix asphalt (HMA) to enhance thermal insulation and delay surface icing through a material-based, environmentally sustainable approach. Marshall mixtures incorporating 5%, 10%, and 20% sawdust at different aggregate size scales were produced and mechanically evaluated to determine the optimum replacement configuration. Based on stability-flow performance and volumetric criteria, filler-scale replacement emerged as the most structurally compatible configuration. Icing delay performance was examined through infrared thermographic analysis and controlled freezing simulations, designed to replicate stepwise cooling conditions on steel bridge-deck thermal behavior. Microstructural and morphological characteristics were assessed using computerized tomography (CT) imaging with image-based segmentation and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and transient thermal analysis (TTA) was employed to quantify effective thermal conductivity. Durability and environmental resistance were evaluated through water sensitivity testing and magnesium sulfate ( MgSO 4 ) cyclic exposure to assess hydrothermal and weathering susceptibility. The results demonstrate that mixtures incorporating 20% filler-sized sawdust maintain adequate mechanical performance while exhibiting enhanced thermal insulation capacity and a remarkable delay in surface freezing relative to the control mixture. Microstructural analyses confirmed homogeneous distribution, effective binder–sawdust interaction, and increased isolated microporosity without disruption of the primary load bearing skeleton. Although bulk thermal conductivity reductions were modest, the combined effects of microstructural modification and transient heat-transfer behavior produced a statistically significant icing-delay response. Overall, the findings indicate that raw wood sawdust can function as a multifunctional ecomaterial, simultaneously contributing to waste and by-product valorization, thermal performance enhancement, and passive anti-icing capability. This study proposes a novel, low-cost, and environmentally responsible material strategy for improving winter road safety, particularly for bridge decks and other icing-prone pavement infrastructures.

The results demonstrate that mixtures incorporating 20% filler-sized sawdust maintain adequate mechanical performance while exhibiting enhanced thermal insulation capacity and a remarkable delay in surface freezing relative to the control mixture. Overall, the findings indicate that raw wood sawdust can function as a multifunctional ecomaterial, simultaneously contributing to waste and by-product valorization, thermal performance enhancement, and passive anti-icing capability.

papers.title: Resistance mutation supply modulates the benefit of CRISPR immunity against virulent phages in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
papers.abstract: Abstract Only a fraction of bacterial genomes encode CRISPR-Cas systems but the selective causes of this variation are unexplained. How naturally virulent bacteriophages (phages) select for CRISPR immunity has rarely been tested experimentally. Here, we show against a panel of genetically and functionally diverse virulent phages that CRISPR immunity was not universally beneficial to Pseudomonas aeruginosa , and its fitness effect varied strongly between phages in predictable ways. In addition to mechanisms known to alter the effectiveness of CRISPR immunity, such as encoding a matching spacer or a protective nuclear shell, we show that the fitness effect of CRISPR immunity negatively associated with the probability of evolving receptor-based resistance to the phage via spontaneous mutation. Supply of resistance mutations differed strongly between very closely related lipopolysaccharide-binding phages and was associated with variation at the C-terminus of the tail fibre protein altering residues involved in hydrogen bonding and the predicted binding site. Our results show that CRISPR immunity is more beneficial against virulent phages that are harder to evolve resistance to via receptor mutations, suggesting that virulent phage community composition and diversity will be important drivers of the prevalence of CRISPR immunity.

papers.title: Endogenous rhythms in deep-sea mussel cell culture and molecular clock characterization
papers.abstract: Abstract While biological rhythms are crucial to life, the deep sea has long been considered an arrhythmic exception. However, at hydrothermal vents - devoid of diel cues yet shaped by tides - the mussel Bathymodiolus azoricus shows both tidal and, unexpectedly, circadian rhythms at -1700 m. Whether endogenous clock(s) drive these cycles remained unanswered. Here, we report endogenous circadian rhythms in B. azoricus cell cultures under constant conditions: isolated cells display a circadian oscillation despite tidal-dominant rhythms in the natural environment. Reporter assays using genomic regions upstream of the mussel’s per gene and containing E-box motifs suggest that a functional transcription–translation feedback loop (TTFL) contributes to circadian timing even in the deep sea. In mussels, BazPeriod lacks autonomous repressive activity but modulates BazCry2 . As BazPeriod itself oscillates tidally, it may explain how a single endogenous clock yields both tidal and diel rhythms. The work also spotlights the highly time-sensitive biology of the vastly unexplored deep-sea environment.

papers.title: Entropic analysis of time series through kernel density estimation
papers.abstract: Abstract This work presents a novel framework for time series analysis using entropic measures based on the kernel density estimate (KDE) of a time series' Takens' embedding in two dimensions. Using this framework we introduce two distinct analytical tools: (1) a multi-scale KDE entropy metric, denoted as $\Delta\text{KE}$, which quantifies the evolution of time series complexity across different delay time scales by measuring changes in entropy, and (2) a sliding baseline method that employs the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence to detect changes in time series structure through changes in KDEs. The $\Delta{\rm KE}$ metric offers insights into the information content and ''unfolding'' properties of the time series' Takens' embedding well-suited to the analysis of dynamical systems, while the KL-divergence-based approach provides a noise and outlier robust measure for identifying time series change points well-suited to the detection of injected radio frequency (RF) signals in noisy backgrounds. We demonstrate the effectiveness and versatility of these tools through a set of experiments across several science and technology domains. In the case of RF communications, we achieve accurate detection of injected signals under varying noise and interference conditions comparable with tools of the art and without the need for training. Secondly, we apply our methodology to electrocardiography (ECG) data, successfully identifying instances of ventricular fibrillation with high accuracy. Finally, we demonstrate the potential of our tools for identifying anomalous intermittent chaotic regimes within a signal in dynamical systems.

papers.title: A systematic review of research issues with Levels of Automation (LOA)
papers.abstract: This systematic review critically analyzes the contexts and challenges of Levels of Automation (LOA), particularly in light of advancements by Artificial Intelligence (AI). Human–automation interaction (HAI) seeks to understand how humans interact with automated systems, particularly as increasing automation places operators increasingly out of the loop. A foundational framework within this field is the Levels of Automation (LOA) framework, which characterizes the respective roles and capabilities of human operators and automated systems. As AI becomes increasingly integrated into traditional HAI applications, a renewed examination of the current state of LOA is warranted. This systematic review examines the following research question: What research demographics, contexts, and challenges associated with LOA are reported in the literature? Data analysis, extraction, and open and axial coding were employed, and consensus was reached by iterative discussion between the authors. The review ultimately included 118 studies. The review identified six contextual categories and 26 challenge codes. The findings provide a comprehensive analysis of the evolving landscape of human–automation interaction. The contribution of this work is to outline weaknesses embedded in research with LOA and suggest a reform with prospects of enhanced HAI with AI.

papers.title: Investigating the transition in ice dynamics from a land- to lake-terminating glacier using a simple glacier dynamics model
papers.abstract: Abstract. Glaciers interact with adjacent proglacial lakes through a range of thermomechanical processes. These interactions occur in addition to climate-driven ablation and are capable of amplifying or modifying climatic effects through various feedback mechanisms. In particular, the connection between lake water-level and the subglacial hydrological system can reduce basal friction, which in turn leads to increased glacier flow and dynamic thinning. This creates a positive feedback loop in which decreased effective pressure, also driven potentially by negative surface mass balance, enhances flow velocity, in line with similar processes observed at marine-terminating glaciers. Our aim in this study is to develop a simple model that can be used to understand the critical controls on the dynamic behaviour of glaciers as they transition from land- to lake-terminating systems. Here, we investigate the behaviour of Skaftafellsjökull in Iceland, which has undergone such a transition over the past twenty-five years. More specifically, we use the Shallow Shelf Approximation (SSA) in Elmer Ice to model ice dynamics, incorporating a water pressure-dependant friction law to model basal sliding with a simple parameterization of basal water pressure. The model successfully reproduces the observed velocity patterns, capturing the shift from downstream deceleration near the front in 2010 to slight acceleration in 2018, reflecting the growing influence of the proglacial lake. We find a threshold behaviour between basal water pressure and ice velocity, whereby small increases in water pressure beyond a critical value led to strong acceleration, consistent with previous empirical observations. Furthermore, our results imply that surface thinning exerts a stronger control on the near terminus acceleration than the observed terminus retreat. Our results suggest that the modelling framework developed provides a valuable tool for simulating these complex interactions in a computationally efficient manner.

Our results suggest that the modelling framework developed provides a valuable tool for simulating these complex interactions in a computationally efficient manner.

papers.title: Kinematic and Dynamical Properties of Solar-neighborhood White Dwarfs from SDSS Data Release 19 and Gaia Data Release 3
papers.abstract: Abstract We present a comprehensive kinematic and dynamical analysis of 5837 white dwarfs with hydrogen-rich atmospheres, SDSS DR19 spectroscopy, and Gaia Data Release 3 astrometry. Using complementary spatial distributions, kinematic properties, and orbital parameters, we show that the sample is overwhelmingly dominated by the thin disk, with only minor contributions from the thick disk and the halo. Velocity dispersions and orbital eccentricities increase systematically from the thin disk to the halo, reflecting progressively hotter Galactic populations. Total stellar ages available for 4829 white dwarfs reveal a clear age–velocity dispersion relation with power-law indices of 0.06–0.17, confirming that white dwarfs preserve the secular dynamical heating history of the Galactic disk. We derive a thin-disk scale height of 123–229 pc and radial scale length of 3.2–3.5 kpc, while the thick disk has a scale height of 865 pc and contributes approximately 6%–7% of the local stellar density. Reconstructed birth radii indicate that changes in the guiding radii represent an important component of the present-day radial redistribution of nearby white dwarfs, although the relative contributions of radial migration and orbital blurring cannot be uniquely separated from these displacement measures. These results establish white dwarfs as powerful tracers of the kinematic, dynamical, and structural evolution of the Milky Way.

papers.title: การเปรยบเทยบตวทำละลายอนทรยในการสกดทรปแทนทรนจากใบหอมสายพนธ Strobilanthes cusia (Nees) Kuntze
authors: ณัฐพร จันทร์ฉาย
papers.journal: Warasan Wichai Lae Songserm Wichakan Kaset
papers.abstract: This study aimed to compare the extraction efficiency of organic solvents with different polarities, specifically ethanol and dichloromethane, for the extraction of tryptanthrin from the leaves of Strobilanthes cusia (Nees) Kuntze collected from five locations in Phrae Province, Thailand. The samples were extracted by maceration, and the tryptanthrin content was quantified using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). The results demonstrated that both the extraction solvent and sampling location significantly affected the amount of tryptanthrin obtained. Overall, dichloromethane yielded higher tryptanthrin contents than ethanol at all sampling sites, and the sample collected from Ban Natong exhibited the highest tryptanthrin content (4.332 mg g-1 crude extract). These findings support the suitability of dichloromethane as an effective solvent for the extraction of tryptanthrin from S. cusia leaves and highlight the importance of raw material origin in determining the level of bioactive compounds. The results provide baseline information for selecting appropriate plant sources and optimizing extraction conditions for future industrial applications.

papers.title: Sensitivity analysis of a solar-biomass hybrid cooler with artificial neural network and engineering equation solver
papers.journal: Energy Sustainable Development/Energy for sustainable development
papers.abstract: To improve the hybrid renewable cooling system, it is necessary to test the effects of additional key operational factors on its performance. In this study, a comprehensive sensitivity analysis of a solar-biomass thermoelectric-adsorption cooler was conducted to establish the priority of the effects of design and operational parameters on the system efficiency using high-fidelity EES simulation and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) surrogate modelling. The thermodynamic model of the hybrid system was created using the Engineering Equation Solver (EES). A Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) plan was employed to create 50 input parameter variations (solar irradiance, fuel biomass, TE current, and adsorption cycle duration). The System Coefficient of Performance (COP) was predicted by the EES model for every combination, producing COP values that ranged from 0.6036 to 0.6307 with a mean of 0.6143. Then, this functionally trained and efficient ANN surrogate model can predict the COP rapidly without hundreds of costly calls to the computationally intensive EES. The ANN model achieved strong prediction performance, with an overall Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 2.12 × 10 − 6 , a correlation coefficient (R) of 0.99478 and a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of approximately 0.9896 for the complete dataset. Sensitivity analysis performed using ANN examines the effect of the system parameters. Within the investigated design space, permutation-based sensitivity analysis ranked biomass feed rate highest in normalised importance (42.3%), followed by adsorption-cycle time (31.2%), solar irradiance (17.6%) and thermoelectric (TE) current (8.9%). These percentages describe the relative importance assigned by the ANN-based analysis. Overall, this study provides a strong correlation and significant sensitivity analysis. Furthermore, an integrated detailed regression analysis supports the ANN surrogate for an efficient design sensitivity evaluation. Calculations from the study showed that the thermal component (adsorption cycle) operation contributes the most to the overall system efficiency, whereas the impact of the electrical components (TE current) diminishes at high load values. The trained ANN provides predictions on a millisecond timescale, substantially reducing the computational burden associated with repeated EES simulations and supporting rapid design-space screening and sensitivity analysis. The maximum observed COP among the 50 simulated cases is 0.630744608 at run 18, corresponding to a biomass rate of 0.000222222 kg/s and an adsorption-cycle time of 81.99 min. The research findings offer a platform for maximum efficiency optimization for future experimental and smart hybrid cooling system development.

Calculations from the study showed that the thermal component (adsorption cycle) operation contributes the most to the overall system efficiency, whereas the impact of the electrical components (TE current) diminishes at high load values. The research findings offer a platform for maximum efficiency optimization for future experimental and smart hybrid cooling system development.

papers.title: Unsaturated fatty acid metabolism and FADS2 as candidate factors in triple-negative breast cancer
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is aggressive and lacks effective targeted therapies. Using estrogen receptor (ER)-negative breast cancer as a proxy for TNBC, we explored circulating metabolite associations and downstream candidate genes. A two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis used large-scale metabolome genome-wide association study data (~1,400 metabolites). Candidate metabolites underwent Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment. Computationally predicted targets were intersected with common differentially expressed genes from three Gene Expression Omnibus datasets and Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis modules. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator-Cox and random survival forest prioritized genes in the Cancer Genome Atlas–TNBC. Single-cell RNA-seq (GSE176078) explored heterogeneity and pathways. MR identified 38 candidate metabolites nominally associated with ER-negative breast cancer risk, enriched in unsaturated fatty acid and arachidonic acid metabolism. Integration yielded 39 candidate genes, and survival-based machine learning prioritized KRAS, MGST3, FADS2, UGT8, IDO1, and SRC. Single-cell analysis showed higher FADS2 in a presumed malignant epithelial subpopulation (log2FC = 2.53, false discovery rate < 0.05), associated with cholesterol biosynthesis, sterol metabolism, and cell-cycle programs. These exploratory findings nominate abnormal circulating unsaturated fatty acid metabolism and FADS2 as candidate factors in ER-negative/TNBC biology. FADS2 is a candidate biomarker and potential target requiring TNBC-specific genetic, patient-aware single-cell, prognostic, and experimental validation.

papers.title: Source-dependent structural and pH-responsive swelling properties of bentonite/cellulose/alginate hydrogel beads derived from agricultural biomass residues
papers.abstract: Agricultural biomass residues are abundant and renewable feedstocks for the development of cellulose-based functional biomaterials. However, direct comparisons of cellulose-rich fractions derived from multiple agricultural biomass sources within the same hydrogel formulation and under identical fabrication conditions remain limited. This study investigated the structural and swelling properties of bentonite/cellulose/alginate (BT/CL/ALG) hydrogel beads prepared from eight agricultural residues: coffee pulp, mango leaf, corn cob, corn leaf, corn husk, corn stalk, sugarcane leaf, and bagasse. The biomass residues were subjected to combined alkaline hydrogen peroxide (AHP) pretreatment to obtain cellulose-rich fractions, which were subsequently incorporated into a sodium alginate matrix with bentonite clay and crosslinked with Ca²⁺. The resulting materials were characterized by compositional analysis, FTIR, XRD, SEM, and TGA/DTG. AHP pretreatment resulted in substantial cellulose enrichment, with the highest cellulose contents observed in corn stalk (76.0%) and bagasse (70.4%). FTIR and XRD analyses indicated changes in the chemical structure and relative crystalline organization of the biomass following pretreatment, while SEM revealed source-dependent morphological changes. The resulting hydrogel beads exhibited differences in swelling behavior, with swelling capacities measured at 144 h ranging from 218.57% to 419.83% in deionized water. Under PBS conditions, all hydrogel beads exhibited pH-responsive swelling, with greater swelling at pH 9 than at pH 3. The highest swelling capacity was observed for the corn-leaf-derived hydrogel at pH 9 (2245.85%). Overall, the findings demonstrate that agricultural biomass residues can provide cellulose-rich feedstocks for the preparation of BT/CL/ALG hydrogel beads with source-dependent structural and swelling characteristics.
papers.summary: Agricultural biomass residues are abundant and renewable feedstocks for the development of cellulose-based functional biomaterials. FTIR and XRD analyses indicated changes in the chemical structure and relative crystalline organization of the biomass following pretreatment, while SEM revealed source-dependent morphological changes. Overall, the findings demonstrate that agricultural biomass residues can provide cellulose-rich feedstocks for the preparation of BT/CL/ALG hydrogel beads with source-dependent structural and swelling characteristics.

papers.title: Hybrid resorbable anchors/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers for enhanced pedicle screw fixation
papers.abstract: Pedicle screw loosening remains a challenge for surgeons and patients. We propose using hybrid resorbable anchors and drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers to enhance the bone fixation of pedicle screws. Polylactide (PLA) anchors with various designs were fabricated using additive manufacturing, while simvastatin- and bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanofibers were prepared through coaxial electrospinning. The effects of PLA anchors and drug/biomolecule-loaded PLGA nanofibrous membranes on improving the pullout strength of pedicle screws from artificial bones were investigated. The in vitro release characteristics of simvastatin and BMP-2 from the nanofibers were evaluated using high-performance liquid chromatography and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, while the in vivo elution of simvastatin was assessed in a rabbit model with histological examinations. The results demonstrate that electrospun drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers, when wrapped around pedicle screws, enhance the screws’ pullout strength. Additionally, the nanofiber/screw system provides a sustained release of simvastatin and BMP-2 for over 30 days in vitro and 4 weeks in vivo. Histological analysis also confirmed the biocompatibility of nanofibrous anchors. Hybrid resorbable anchors and drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers show potential for improving screw fixation and serving as a platform for extended drug delivery.

The results demonstrate that electrospun drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers, when wrapped around pedicle screws, enhance the screws’ pullout strength.

papers.title: Revealing a pressure-induced reversible polymorph transformation by monitoring in-die density during powder compression
papers.abstract: Abstract The reversible pressure-induced phase transformation of urea during powder compaction was investigated using a compaction simulator. The reversible change in solid density observed between 600 MPa and 900 MPa is consistent with the known pressure-induced reversible phase transformation between urea forms I and III. These findings establish compaction simulation as a material-sparing method for detecting pressure-induced phase transformations of active pharmaceutical ingredients during tableting, provided that the density change due to the polymorphic form transition is sufficiently large.

papers.title: Mechanistic understanding of the precipitation inhibition effect of HPMCAS via thermodynamic modeling
papers.abstract: Abstract Understanding the precipitation risk of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) in amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs) is still a major challenge in their development. In a previous study (Nakhla et al., Int. J. Pharm. X, 11, 2026, 100475) (Nakhla et al. 2026), we demonstrated the dual functionality of HPMCAS in high drug-load nifedipine (NIF) ASD tablets prepared by hot-melt extrusion, where HPMCAS-H acted both as an effective dry binder and as a precipitation inhibitor. While the experimental data clearly showed prolonged supersaturation and improved tablet performance upon addition of HPMCAS-H, the thermodynamic origin of this precipitation inhibition remained unresolved. The present work directly builds upon these findings and provides a mechanistic interpretation of the observed release behavior using thermodynamic modeling. The dissolution behavior of binary NIF ASDs with either PVP-VA64 (a fully water-soluble polymer) or HPMCAS (a water-dispersible polymer) was analyzed with and without pre-dispersed polymers. Under the conditions investigated, both systems generated initial apparent supersaturation, followed by rapid loss of filter-passing NIF for PVP-VA64-based ASDs. Pre-dispersed PVP-VA64 and HPC-EXF did not prevent this decrease in the present NIF system. In contrast, pre-dispersed HPMCAS-H suppressed or substantially delayed the loss of filter-passing NIF, consistent with its stabilizing effect in ASD tablets. To rationalize these differences, ternary NIF/polymer/water phase diagrams were predicted using PC-SAFT. The calculations support formation of an HPMCAS-H-rich liquid/polymer-rich phase that can accommodate NIF and may manifest experimentally as a colloidal dispersion. Effective stabilization therefore depends on the specific balance of API-polymer and polymer-water interactions captured by the ternary phase diagrams.
papers.summary: Abstract Understanding the precipitation risk of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) in amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs) is still a major challenge in their development. While the experimental data clearly showed prolonged supersaturation and improved tablet performance upon addition of HPMCAS-H, the thermodynamic origin of this precipitation inhibition remained unresolved. To rationalize these differences, ternary NIF/polymer/water phase diagrams were predicted using PC-SAFT.

papers.abstract: This study investigates the preparation and properties of poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) composites reinforced with bagasse fibers, focusing on the effects of fiber loading (10–30 pph) and alkaline surface treatment on the mechanical, morphological, and thermo-mechanical properties of the composites. The fibers were treated with 5 wt.% sodium hydroxide solution, then compounded with PBS using a twin-screw extruder and hot-compression molding to produce test specimens. Morphological analysis revealed that the alkali-treated fibers exhibited a cleaner and rougher surface than untreated fibers, which was consistent with the FTIR results showing a reduction in the intensity of peaks associated with hemicellulose, lignin, and surface impurities. The incorporation of bagasse fibers increased the tensile modulus and heat deflection temperature (HDT) of the composites with increasing fiber content. The tensile modulus increased from 325.3 MPa for neat PBS to 955.4 MPa, while the HDT increased from 87.6°C to 108.3°C for the composite containing 30 pph alkali-treated fibers. However, tensile strength, percent elongation at break, and impact strength gradually decreased as fiber loading increased because of stress concentration and reduced matrix continuity. Alkali treatment improved the interfacial adhesion between the fibers and the PBS matrix, resulting in higher tensile strength and impact strength than those of composites containing untreated fibers. In addition, fiber incorporation had only a slight influence on the thermal behavior and overall crystallinity of PBS. These findings demonstrate that alkali-treated sugarcane bagasse fibers are promising reinforcing materials for PBS, providing enhanced stiffness and heat deflection resistance while offering a sustainable approach for valorizing agricultural waste in the development of biodegradable biocomposites.

papers.title: The use of sheep’s wool from the Kyrgyz Republic as a component of a fertiliser composite: incubation studies
papers.abstract: There is currently growing interest in reusing various types of waste in the economy, in order to avoid unnecessary costs and improve the environmental sustainability of materials. One such material is sheep wool, which is considered waste in some parts of Asia and Europe. The aim of this study was to investigate the physicochemical properties of sheep wool sourced from the Kyrgyz Republic, to use it to develop a fertiliser and assess its initial behaviour in the soil. Using wool fibre, a fertiliser based on a polymer matrix was produced, and an analysis of the fibre’s elemental composition was carried out, along with a thermal analysis of the fertiliser before and after incubation in soil to assess the degree of degradation, and a basic analysis of the soil following the incubation process. The wool studied is characterised by a high nitrogen content, accelerates the degradation of the fertiliser and can serve as a carrier for additional minerals. The presence of the fertiliser in the soil alters its properties, and these changes are more gradual than with mineral fertilisers, leading to less soil degradation. The use of wool as a fertiliser component means that it can act as a slow-release agent and form the basis for further research into waste materials for use in agriculture.

papers.abstract: งานวิจัยนี้ศึกษาแอคติโนมัยซีทส่งเสริมการเจริญของพืชจากดินรอบรากข้าวใน 6 อำเภอของจังหวัดพระนครศรีอยุธยา เพื่อเป็นแนวทางในการใช้จุลินทรีย์ทดแทนสารเคมีและเพิ่มมูลค่าผลผลิต จากการคัดแยกแอคติโนมัยซีท 111 ไอโซเลท พบไอโซเลทที่ละลายฟอสเฟต ผลิตกรดอินโดลอะซิติก (IAA) และเจริญบนอาหารไร้ไนโตรเจนจำนวน 24, 106 และ 66 ไอโซเลท ตามลำดับ ไอโซเลท RS5A07 มีดัชนีละลายฟอสเฟตสูงสุด (2.46±0.05) พร้อมทั้งสร้าง IAA และเจริญบนอาหารไร้ไนโตรเจนได้ และไอโซเลท RS4A07 เจริญเติบโตเร็วและผลิต IAA ได้สูง (35.03±0.74 ไมโครกรัมต่อมิลลิลิตร) จากการวิเคราะห์ยีน 16S rRNA ระบุว่า RS5A07 และ RS4A07 คล้ายคลึงกับ Streptomyces viridiviolaceus (99 เปอร์เซ็นต์) และ Saccharopolyspora endophytica (99 เปอร์เซ็นต์) ตามลำดับ การทดสอบประสิทธิภาพการส่งเสริมการเจริญของข้าวแบ่งเป็น 4 กลุ่ม ได้แก่ กลุ่มควบคุม (ไม่เติมหัวเชื้อ) กลุ่มเติม RS5A07 กลุ่มเติม RS4A07 และกลุ่มเติมหัวเชื้อผสม (105 โคโลนีต่อมิลลิลิตร ปริมาตร 200 มิลลิลิตร ทุก 15 วัน) พบว่าหลังปลูก 26 วัน ข้าวกลุ่มเติมหัวเชื้อมีอัตราการเติบโตสูงกว่ากลุ่มควบคุม หลัง 50 วันกลุ่มเติมหัวเชื้อผสมมีความยาวรากมากที่สุดอย่างมีนัยสำคัญทางสถิติ แต่ทุกกลุ่มทดลองไม่พบความแตกต่างอย่างมีนัยสำคัญทางสถิติในด้านความยาวต้น น้ำหนักสดและแห้งของลำต้นและราก รวมถึงปริมาณคลอโรฟิลล์ ดังนั้น แอคติโนมัยซีทจากการศึกษานี้ยังไม่สามารถเพิ่มอัตราการเจริญของต้นข้าวในระยะ 50 วันได้ แต่การใช้จุลินทรีย์หลายสายพันธุ์สามารถเพิ่มความยาวรากได้ ซึ่งจำเป็นต้องเพิ่มระยะเวลาในการศึกษา และปรับรูปแบบการใช้หัวเชื้อร่วมด้วย

papers.title: Alkyl Imidazolium Cation-Supported Poly(terphenyl- co -fluorene isatin) Anion Exchange Membrane for Anion Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Anion exchange membrane (AEM) is the core component of alkaline fuel cells. Current research still faces bottlenecks such as the difficulty in synergizing ion conductivity and alkali stability, and the inhibition of reaction kinetics by adsorption of ionomer catalysts. In this work, a new ether-free poly(terphenyl-co-fluorene isatin) polymer backbone was developed. Alkyl imidazole with a unique π-conjugated delocalized structure was selected as a cation to develop a series of imidazole cation-loaded comb-shaped poly(terphenyl-co-fluorene isatin) polyelectrolytes (PTFI-IZ-n). The additional hydrophobic structure on the imidazole cation provides a driving force for the self-assembly of ion clusters. PTFI-IZ-8 AEM exhibits the most developed phase separation morphology and exhibits a high OH– conductivity of 140.61 mS/cm at 80 °C. The long comb-like alkyl chain in PTFI-IZ-8 AEM effectively protects the stability of the cation. After 1200 h in 2 M NaOH at 80 °C, the ion conductivity only decreased by 10.32% and the tensile strength decreased by 11.05%. The peak power density of H2–O2 AEMFC based on PTFI-IZ-8 can reach 1.03 W/cm2 at 80 °C, providing a new strategy for the design of high-performance anion exchange membranes.

The peak power density of H2–O2 AEMFC based on PTFI-IZ-8 can reach 1.03 W/cm2 at 80 °C, providing a new strategy for the design of high-performance anion exchange membranes.

papers.title: Cation-Intercalated Mott Insulator α-RuCl3 Superlattice for Actively Tuned Optoelectronics
papers.abstract: Abstract Active tuning of the spectral response within sensing materials is critical for application-specific optoelectronics. However, current approaches typically suffer from limited tunability, complex architectures, or sacrificed stability. Here we report an on-chip cation intercalation strategy that transforms the Kitaev-candidate Mott insulator α-ruthenium chloride (α-RuCl3) into a tetramethylammonium (TMA+)-intercalated RuCl3 layered superlattice. The intercalation-induced reconstruction of the Mott-derived electronic states substantially narrows the optical gap from ∼1.1 eV to ∼0.6 eV, extending the spectral response into the short-wave infrared (SWIR) regime. The introduction of an in situ van der Waals tunneling barrier suppresses dark current by >3 orders of magnitude and enhances specific detectivity by 4–6 orders of magnitude. By employing machine learning models, we demonstrate device-response-guided image processing for intelligent recognition under degraded environments. This work establishes a connection between correlated-electron systems and intelligent sensing, stimulating research directions at the intersection of quantum materials, optoelectronics, and intelligent sensing systems.

papers.title: Photodegradation versus network densification in UV-cured PolyJet 3D-printed polymers: A structure-mechanics study
papers.abstract: PolyJet™ 3D printing of MED610™ photopolymer is increasingly used for dental and prosthetic structures; however, the coupled effects of in-plane printing direction and post-curing temperature on network evolution, photooxidation, and mechanical durability remain insufficiently understood. Herein, MED610 specimens were printed in two horizontal orientations (X and Y) and post-cured at room temperature or 64 °C to establish a chemistry-based structure-property relationship. The Y-oriented specimens exhibited lower roughness and pore-like defects than the X-oriented specimens, leading to improved tensile and flexural performance. The room-temperature post-curing enhanced interlayer bonding and increased flexural stress by approximately 8.5% compared with the untreated Y-oriented sample, while maintaining tensile strength. In contrast, UV post-curing at 64 °C caused substantial deterioration, reducing tensile stress, flexural stress, flexural modulus, wear resistance, and effective network integrity. FTIR and XPS confirmed post-curing-induced surface chemical changes, with the O 1 s/C 1s atomic ratio increasing from 0.13 to 0.21 after 64 °C treatment, indicating enhanced surface oxidation. DMA further revealed that room-temperature post-curing increased Tg and effective crosslink density, whereas 64 °C treatment produced the lowest storage modulus and effective crosslink density. These results support a competition between beneficial network densification/interlayer strengthening at room temperature and UV-assisted photooxidative degradation within the glass-transition region at 64 °C. This work distinguishes itself from previous processing-focused studies by linking PolyJet horizontal orientation and post-curing temperature to molecular-level network evolution, surface oxidation, and wear-mechanical performance, providing guidance for optimising MED610-based dental structures within the tested conditions.
